name: Carnegie Mellon University
degree_name: B.S. in Robotics (School of Computer Science; declare end of first year)
degree_type: Dedicated primary robotics bachelor’s degree; additional major, non-SCS minor and SCS concentration are separate credentials [CMU-R26-9][CMU-R26-11]
program_archetype: Primary robotics engineering with supporting AI
major_access_full: Apply to the School of Computer Science, then declare BSR after first year. Non-SCS transfer is competitive: 3.0 overall QPA, 3.6 across six specified courses, essay and available space. The Robotics Additional Major is a separate credential.
recommended_major_route: Apply to SCS with the primary B.S. in Robotics as the goal, then declare during the first year. [CMU-R26-2]
alternative_route: BS Electrical and Computer Engineering (College of Engineering, direct admit) + Additional Major in Robotics
primary_structural_risk: SCS admission is the first-year route. Admission to another college does not secure a BSR transfer; ECE plus an Additional Major has different GPA, prerequisite and seat constraints.
notable_ai_institute: Robotics Institute, Machine Learning Department, Language Technologies Institute, HCII (all own AI-cluster courses) [CMU-S1]
notable_undergraduate_research_program: SURF ($4,500, first-years eligible) and SCS Honors Thesis 07-599 (no GPA requirement) [CMU-S14][CMU-S13]
fourplusone_name: SCS Fifth-Year Master's / Accelerated Master's (BSAI eligible with added CS breadth) [CMU-S24][CMU-S25]
housing_guarantee: Four-year guarantee for students continuously in university housing; first-years required on campus; 65% stay on campus all four years [CMU-S38][CMU-S39]
sports_influence: Minor / prominent but optional (INFERRED, weakly evidenced)
recreation_center: Cohon University Center fitness center (10,000 sq ft, two stories) + Wiegand Gym + pools [CMU-S43]
best_fit_reason: A primary Robotics BS with required robot building, feedback control, kinematics, vision, and a two-course systems/capstone sequence. Three robotics electives and an SCS elective support planning and learning alongside real hardware.
biggest_concern: The SCS admission hurdle and substantial cost. The historic 2015 SCS admit rate is not a current robotics admission probability.
evidence_confidence: Official curriculum and entry sources reviewed October 14, 2026; recommendations and 1–5 scores are analyst assessments. Future seats, unpublished cohort rules and some source conflicts remain unresolved.

score_notes.cs_foundations: BSR requires 15-122, 15-213 and 15-251 plus mathematical foundations; the old five-course BSAI CS spine is not the BSR core.
score_notes.math_foundations: Calculus 21-120/122, linear algebra 21-241, 16-211 Foundational Mathematics of Robotics, 15-151/21-127, and an approved probability choice.
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: Required controls 16-299 includes planning and reinforcement learning; 16-385 covers vision. Elective candidates include 10-315 ML for SCS undergraduates, 16-350 planning and 10-403 deep RL; slot approval and prerequisites still apply.
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Supporting AI is elective depth within B.S. in Robotics (School of Computer Science; declare end of first year). 16-385 Computer Vision; 16-350 Planning Techniques for Robotics; 10-403 Deep Reinforcement Learning & Control; 10-315 Introduction to Machine Learning (SCS Majors). Check the stated prerequisites, permissions and degree-credit rules; these courses are not all required or guaranteed.
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: The reviewed undergraduate options emphasize perception, machine learning and planning for robotics. Graduate institute topics or an alternative AI-major core are not counted as required coursework.
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: The recommended route has its own degree requirements, elective slots and minor-overlap rules. Confirm that each AI or robotics elective counts toward this specific degree; university-wide availability is insufficient.
score_notes.course_availability: Catalog labels are current evidence, not future schedules: 16-220/384/450 Fall, 16-299/350/474 Spring, 16-385 Fall and Spring. Future terms and elective seats require advising.
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: BSR permits up to 12 units of 16-597 or 99-270 and an optional SCS Honors thesis; mentor selection and seats are not guaranteed.
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: 07-300/07-400 research courses sit inside the major and faculty run public 07-280/07-380 course sites, but no central lab-matching program was found [CMU-S8][CMU-S9].
score_notes.project_based_learning: Required 16-220 hardware build, 16-299 real robot control work, 16-384 robot-arm programming, and 16-450 → 16-474 system design/integration/testing.
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: Primary BSR guarantees robot building, controls, kinematics, vision and a two-course senior integration project. Additional major, non-SCS minor and SCS concentration are separate routes.
score_notes.computing_resources: No undergraduate-facing GPU or cluster allocation page was verified this session.
score_notes.industry_preparation: General programme preparation context; CS salaries, company bands and graduate institute research are not verified robotics-major placement outcomes. Confirm the selected degree’s graduate option and any eligible co-op/research pathway.
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: General programme preparation context; CS salaries, company bands and graduate institute research are not verified robotics-major placement outcomes. Confirm the selected degree’s graduate option and any eligible co-op/research pathway.
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: General programme preparation context; CS salaries, company bands and graduate institute research are not verified robotics-major placement outcomes. Confirm the selected degree’s graduate option and any eligible co-op/research pathway.
score_notes.intellectual_energy: ~40 student-taught StuCo courses run per term and TartanHacks 2026 was billed as Pittsburgh's largest hackathon [CMU-S23][CMU-S59].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: Students report most CMU classes are not curved and little interpersonal competition, but official/journalistic sources document stress rising to 58% high-risk by finals week [CMU-S67][CMU-S74].
score_notes.student_agency: Undergraduates teach for-credit 98-xxx courses and run a 24/7 machine shop for ~$30/year in dues [CMU-S23][CMU-S51].
score_notes.community_within_scale: SCS has 999 undergraduates inside a 7,824-undergraduate university, and 65% of students live on campus all four years [CMU-S60][CMU-S61][CMU-S38].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: Roboclub dates to 1984 with a machine shop, 3D printers, and laser cutter; ScottyLabs ran TartanHacks Feb 6–7, 2026 [CMU-S51][CMU-S59].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: StuCo offerings include Private Pilot Ground School alongside technical minis, but the full activities directory was not verified [CMU-S23].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Greek life is 19% of the student body (1,100+ members) and does not control housing, since first-years must live on campus and 65% stay four years [CMU-S36][CMU-S38].
score_notes.campus_engagement: Buggy/Sweepstakes has run since 1920 and 2026 Spring Carnival ran April 9–11 with race day April 11 [CMU-S46][CMU-S48].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: Cohon Center offers a 10,000 sq ft, two-story fitness center with 60+ cardio machines, pools, and squash courts, open to all students on CMU ID with 30–35 free weekly Group X classes [CMU-S43][CMU-S41][CMU-S45].

door.how_you_enter: You apply to the College of Engineering and are admitted directly to the ECE department/major (or as CoE undecided); the School of Computer Science is an entirely separate admit unit.
door.easier_than_cs_basis: CMU's first-party admission and SCS undergraduate pages publish no current per-college or per-major admit rates (CMU-E2, CMU-E4), so no published comparison of the CoE/ECE door with the SCS door exists. What is documented is that they are separate doors: 'Students applying to the College of Engineering apply to and are admitted directly to a department/major unless choosing undecided' (CMU-E2).
door.internal_gate: Graduation QPA of 2.0 required after freshman year; ECE department courses require a minimum 2.0 QPA and prerequisite courses require a grade of C or better (18-202 specifically C or better) (CMU-E1). Robotics Additional Major requires a 3.0 GPA to apply and a 3.0 QPA in the additional-major curriculum to graduate (CMU-E3).

ece.vs_cs: ECE at CMU is a genuinely different door from SCS: ECE is admitted through the College of Engineering while CS/AI/Robotics majors are admitted through SCS, and ECE's own course set already covers controls (18-370, 18-474), autonomous robotics (18-442), mechatronics (18-578), vision (18-395, 18-794) and ML for engineers (18-461/18-462). Crucially, an ECE student can still reach the Robotics Additional Major, which is 'Open to students across all majors and colleges at Carnegie Mellon University' at a 3.0 GPA, and the Machine Learning Minor, which is explicitly reserved for undergraduates 'outside the School of Computer Science' — so ECE, not CS, is the major that unlocks the ML minor. The cost is a hardware-heavy core (circuits, devices, 18-220/18-240/18-290) and the fact that CMU publishes no admit-rate evidence that the CoE door is actually easier.
ece.notable: Integrated Master's/Bachelor's (IMB) into the Professional M.S. in ECE is guaranteed at 270+ units with a 3.00 QPA, with no separate application and no GRE (CMU-E1). Robotics Additional Major lets non-CS majors double count up to six courses (CS majors only five) (CMU-E3). The Machine Learning Minor is open to any major outside SCS (CMU-E5).

door.how_you_enter: You apply to Cornell Engineering as your college, not to ECE: 'Cornell University only allows applicants to apply to one of the seven undergraduate colleges and schools' and 'No, you do not apply to a particular major; you apply to the college' — you may indicate an intended major, and 'You do not officially select your major until the second semester of your sophomore year' (CORNELL-E2, CORNELL-E3).
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Cornell publishes admissions decisions at the college level, not by major, and no first-party per-major admit rates for ECE or CS were found. The structural point is that you apply to a college rather than a major, and ECE and Engineering-side CS sit in the same college, so the college choice matters more than the major label (CORNELL-E2).
door.internal_gate: ECE affiliation requires at least a C+ in MATH 2930 or 2940, in PHYS 2213, and in one of ECE 2100/ENGRD 2100, ECE 2720 or ECE 2300/ENGRD 2300, plus a GPA of at least 2.5 across the listed math, physics and ECE gateway courses (CORNELL-E1).

ece.vs_cs: The decisive Cornell fact is that you apply to one of seven colleges and not to a major: Cornell Engineering is the single wrapper for both ECE and Engineering-side CS, so ECE is not a lower-selectivity backdoor but a different major chosen inside the same admitted cohort (major selection happens in the second semester of sophomore year). Once affiliated, ECE gives a hardware-and-signals core (circuits, digital logic, signals, embedded) with a required Culminating Design Experience and hands-on robotics through ECE 4160 Fast Robots, which focuses on 'systems level design and implementation of fast and dynamic autonomous robots' and has students 'design a fast autonomous car, explore dynamic behaviors, acting forces, sensors, and reactive control on an embedded processor'. The costs are a modest affiliation gate (C+ in gateway courses, 2.5 GPA) and the fact that ECE has no formal robotics track — robotics is a listed concentration area rather than a defined thread.
ece.notable: First-years arrive without an official major inside Cornell Engineering and must be 'accepted into and affiliate with a specific Engineering major' (CORNELL-E2). ECE 4160 Fast Robots is cross-listed with ECE 5160, MAE 4190 and MAE 5190, so the robotics course is shared with mechanical engineering (CORNELL-E4). The College of Engineering is now named the Cornell David A. Duffield College of Engineering (CORNELL-E2).

engineering.how_you_enter: You apply on the Common Application to either Trinity College of Arts & Sciences or the Pratt School of Engineering, and ECE exists only inside Pratt while Computer Science exists only inside Trinity, so the ECE-vs-CS decision is made as a college choice at application time.

computing.basis: Computing alternative: Apply to Trinity College of Arts & Sciences; CS is not offered in Pratt. Students declare the major by sophomore spring (the department calls that the ideal time), with no published GPA cutoff or cap. Admission is to Trinity, not to the CS major; declaring is open. The BS has optional concentrations (AI and Machine Learning, Data Science, Software Systems, Software Engineering and Design) but none in robotics. Fall 2026 matriculants must take an AI core course (e.g., COMPSCI 370 or 371 or 527). COMPSCI 590 Robot Learning is a special topic, not a regular course. Trinity students can earn the robotics certificate, but its required ECE 383L needs ECE 280L or EGR 224L, which are engineering courses outside the CS major.

door.how_you_enter: You apply on the Common Application to either Trinity College of Arts & Sciences or the Pratt School of Engineering, and ECE exists only inside Pratt while Computer Science exists only inside Trinity, so the ECE-vs-CS decision is made as a college choice at application time.
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Duke's Class of 2029 profile publishes only a single university-wide funnel (58,712 applications, 5.2% overall, 12.6% Early Decision, 4.2% Regular Decision) with no Trinity-versus-Pratt breakdown, so no per-college or per-major comparison is published (DUKE-E6).
door.internal_gate: None published for declaring ECE once enrolled in Pratt; the ECE BSE requires at least 34 units including six foundation courses (DUKE-E1). Changing between Trinity and Pratt after enrollment is not addressed on the apply page (DUKE-E4).

ece.vs_cs: At Duke, ECE is the only door to robotics hardware: the BSE curriculum forces circuits, digital systems, signals and controls (ECE 110L/230L/250D/270DL/280L) and then lets you stack the ECE Machine Learning concentration on top, so you graduate able to build the sensing-and-actuation stack as well as the model (DUKE-E1, DUKE-E2). CS in Trinity gives more algorithms, theory and software breadth and a lighter math/lab load, but no accredited engineering degree and no required hardware sequence. The real cost is structural, not curricular: choosing ECE means applying to Pratt rather than Trinity on the application itself, and Duke publishes no evidence that either college is the easier admit (DUKE-E4, DUKE-E6).
ece.notable: Duke offers a university-wide Minor in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence administered by ECE (DUKE-E8), an ECE minor, and a Robotics and Automation Certificate that pairs ECE 383 with ME 555 Robot Studio plus machine-learning, controls/dynamics and ethics courses (DUKE-E7). Pratt awards BSE degrees in Biomedical, Civil, Environmental, Mechanical and Electrical & Computer engineering only (DUKE-E5).

admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: REQUIRED. Self-reported scores are accepted and recommended (Common App testing section or the post-submission portal form); scores on transcripts or sent by email/fax/mail are not used. ACT writing and the SAT optional essay are not required. Highest section scores are combined (English/Math/Reading for ACT; EBRW/Math for SAT). CLT scores may be self-reported but do not substitute for SAT/ACT [GT-S4]. Latest acceptable test date per CDS C8E: 23 January [GT-S1].

_raw.test_policy_2027_cycle: REQUIRED. CDS C8 for the 2025-2026 edition states SAT/ACT are 'Required to be considered for admission' for Fall 2027 [GT-S1], and the admissions site states 'All first-year applicants must submit results from at least one SAT and/or ACT in order to be considered for admission' [GT-S4]. Self-reported scores are accepted and recommended (Common App testing section or the post-submission portal form); scores on transcripts or sent by email/fax/mail are not used. ACT writing and the SAT optional essay are not required. Highest section scores are combined (English/Math/Reading for ACT; EBRW/Math for SAT). CLT scores may be self-reported but do not substitute for SAT/ACT [GT-S4]. Latest acceptable test date per CDS C8E: 23 January [GT-S1].

However, on your Common Application, you are asked to select an intended (primary) major' — and 'consideration of your major is an important part of our application review process' (GT-E3).
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Georgia Tech does not publish admit rates by major or college (the first-year class profile page returned no such figures), so no numeric ECE-vs-CS comparison exists. The documented asymmetry is post-admission: 'Due to high-demand, first-year students who are admitted Summer 2024 and beyond will not have the option to confirm their major to the BS in Computer Science' (GT-E4), and the registrar states such students 'will not have the option to change their major to the BS in Computer Science and must plan accordingly' (GT-E5).
door.internal_gate: No published GPA or capacity gate to confirm an ECE major; the restriction runs the other way — CS is a 'space-restricted program' now accepting change-of-major applications only 'on a limited basis', and 'Students should not assume they will be able to change their major to Computer Science' (GT-E7).

ece.vs_cs: At Georgia Tech ECE and CS sit in different colleges (College of Engineering vs College of Computing) and, because major confirmation into the BS CS is closed to students admitted Summer 2024 and later, ECE is the door that stays open — you can confirm or change into EE or Computer Engineering, but not into CS. The ECE thread system is unusually well matched to this applicant: BS EE picks any two of eight threads including Robotics, and BS CmpE picks two of nine including Robotics & Autonomous Systems, backed by ECE 3550/4550 controls, ECE 4560 robotics, ECE 4580 vision, ECE 4252 machine learning and ECE 4180 embedded systems. The cost is that GT publishes no admit-rate evidence, and intended major is explicitly weighed in review, so listing ECE is a real commitment rather than a backdoor.
ece.notable: Georgia Tech CS is CAC-accredited while EE and CmpE are EAC-accredited under the electrical/computer program criteria (GT-E1). ECE also owns robotics-specific graduate courses (ECE 7785 Introduction to Robotics Research, ECE 8741 Robotics Capstone Project) that undergraduates can approach through the BS/MS (GT-E6).

name: Johns Hopkins University
degree_name: BS Computer Engineering + optional Robotics study focus area + LCSR Robotics minor
degree_type: Computer Engineering BS with ECE hardware/signals and CS programming/data structures core, two-term design capstone, optional Robotics study focus area and LCSR minor.
program_archetype: ECE / computer engineering robotics route with supporting AI
major_access_full: Computer Engineering is a primary undergraduate degree in Whiting Engineering. The reviewed catalogue provides its 126-credit plan; programme-specific first-year admission odds and current declaration procedures were not published in the accessible sources. Confirm intended-major procedures with admissions.
recommended_major_route: BS Computer Engineering has the same ECE electronics/signals/design core as EE plus required intermediate programming and data structures. Both have an optional Robotics study focus area and a two-term ECE capstone. Add selectable controls, robot sensors/mechatronics, machine perception, embedded AI and sensor-based robotics; the interdisciplinary minor gives transcript recognition. EE is the controls/sensing alternative and CS is the software/planning alternative. Primary ordering is analyst judgment, not an admissions advantage.
alternative_route: BS Electrical Engineering + Robotics focus area/minor for more controls and sensing; BS Computer Science + Robotics focus area/minor for algorithms, planning and perception, adding engineering control/dynamics courses.
primary_structural_risk: Live CS declaration: SIS form, four-year plan, departmental review and advisor approval; no GPA/cap threshold stated, and secondary-major/minor declarations pause before/during registration. Prior admissions FAQ said university-wide admission except BME, but its current page returns403; preserve as older policy pending re-verification. Confirm elective prerequisites, permissions and degree applicability.
notable_ai_institute: Data Science and AI Institute (150+ affiliated faculty, 22 new hires Aug 2025, director Mark Dredze from Nov 2025); LCSR; CLSP; Institute for Assured Autonomy
notable_undergraduate_research_program: PURA ($3,000 academic year) and Summer PURA ($6,000, 10 weeks; 113 funded in Summer 2025); CSMR REU (LCSR/NSF, US citizens/PRs)
fourplusone_name: Combined (concurrent) BS/MSE in Computer Science; also combined BS/MSE in Robotics via LCSR and concurrent BS/MSSI
housing_guarantee: Two-year residency requirement for first- and second-year students; 93% of first-years in college housing, 46% of all undergraduates
greek_participation: 25% of men join fraternities, 21% of women join sororities (CDS 2025-2026); ~1,300-1,400 students across 25 organizations
sports_influence: UNK — NCAA Division III (except lacrosse) was not verified in this session; the O'Connor indoor track closes during varsity practices [JHU-S28]
recreation_center: Ralph S. O'Connor Center for Recreation & Well-Being (free to Homewood students)
best_fit_reason: BS Computer Engineering has the same ECE electronics/signals/design core as EE plus required intermediate programming and data structures. Both have an optional Robotics study focus area and a two-term ECE capstone. Add selectable controls, robot sensors/mechatronics, machine perception, embedded AI and sensor-based robotics; the interdisciplinary minor gives transcript recognition. EE is the controls/sensing alternative and CS is the software/planning alternative. Primary ordering is analyst judgment, not an admissions advantage.
biggest_concern: There is no robotics degree on the diploma, and ECE puts little weight on mechanical kinematics/dynamics. He would need ME courses such as EN.530.420/421 to fill that part of the minor, inside a fairly full 126-credit plan.
evidence_confidence: Official curriculum and entry sources reviewed October 14, 2026; recommendations and 1–5 scores are analyst assessments. Future seats, unpublished cohort rules and some source conflicts remain unresolved.

score_notes.cs_foundations: Programming and software foundations are assessed in the recommended BS Computer Engineering + optional Robotics study focus area + LCSR Robotics minor plan. This is not the former CS/AI major; use the home-department core and the prerequisites on Robotics routes.
score_notes.math_foundations: Check calculus, linear algebra, probability and differential-equation preparation against the recommended engineering plan and the controls/learning prerequisites. Do not substitute the former CS/AI major requirements.
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: Supporting options for the recommended route: EN.520.465 Machine Perception; EN.520.440 Machine Intelligence on Embedded Systems; EN.601.461 Computer Vision; EN.601.464 Artificial Intelligence; EN.520.241 Introduction to Mechatronics: Sensing, Processing, Learning and Actuation. Prerequisites, permissions and degree credit restrictions are recorded on Robotics routes.
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Supporting AI is elective depth within BS Computer Engineering + optional Robotics study focus area + LCSR Robotics minor. EN.520.465 Machine Perception; EN.520.440 Machine Intelligence on Embedded Systems; EN.601.461 Computer Vision; EN.601.464 Artificial Intelligence; EN.520.241 Introduction to Mechatronics: Sensing, Processing, Learning and Actuation. Check the stated prerequisites, permissions and degree-credit rules; these courses are not all required or guaranteed.
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: The reviewed undergraduate options emphasize perception, machine learning and planning for robotics. Graduate institute topics or an alternative AI-major core are not counted as required coursework.
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: The recommended route has its own degree requirements, elective slots and minor-overlap rules. Confirm that each AI or robotics elective counts toward this specific degree; university-wide availability is insufficient.
score_notes.course_availability: Future course offerings, seats and permissions are not guaranteed; current catalogue listings and published annual/every-other-year categories are recorded separately.
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: Official participation claims range from 65% to over 90%, but an official HOUR deck states 80% of undergraduate researchers are entirely uncompensated volunteers [JHU-S13][JHU-S15][JHU-S38].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: The 9:1 student-faculty ratio and 22 new DSAI faculty hired in August 2025 expand capacity, but HOUR's own guidance is cold-email outreach with 3-4 follow-ups [JHU-S25][JHU-S8][JHU-S38].
score_notes.project_based_learning: Home-department design/capstone and documented robotics course projects support this route. The Laboratory for Computational Sensing and Robotics (LCSR) anchors robotics at JHU, with medical robotics as a major strength. Undergrad teams include the Johns Hopkins Robotics Club, whose members can get access to the LCSR Robotorium, and the Hopkinauts Mars Rover Team, which competes in the University Rover Challenge. A robotics lab or industry sponsor does not guarantee an undergraduate position.
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: Robotics Minor; 13 undergrad robotics courses. 17 labs, LCSR, 1 competition team.
score_notes.computing_resources: Rockfish offers 45,072 cores and 32 A100/L40S GPU nodes, but accounts activate only after a PI with an approved allocation adds the user [JHU-S32][JHU-S33].
score_notes.industry_preparation: General programme preparation context; CS salaries, company bands and graduate institute research are not verified robotics-major placement outcomes. Confirm the selected degree’s graduate option and any eligible co-op/research pathway.
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: General programme preparation context; CS salaries, company bands and graduate institute research are not verified robotics-major placement outcomes. Confirm the selected degree’s graduate option and any eligible co-op/research pathway.
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: General programme preparation context; CS salaries, company bands and graduate institute research are not verified robotics-major placement outcomes. Confirm the selected degree’s graduate option and any eligible co-op/research pathway.
score_notes.intellectual_energy: HopHacks runs every semester and its September 12-14, 2025 edition drew nearly 300 participants from 57 universities with a record 102 projects [JHU-S21].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: No current multi-source student evidence on competitiveness or pressure was collected, and the brief forbids inferring it from structure.
score_notes.student_agency: A CS major can declare via an SIS request plus an advisor-approved four-year plan, and can substitute a 600-level course for a 400-level one in the robotics minor without an exception form [JHU-S1][JHU-S3].
score_notes.community_within_scale: 5,679 full-time undergraduates with a mandatory two-year on-campus residency requirement and 93% of first-years in college housing [JHU-S25][JHU-S26].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: The CS department lists nine student groups including HopAI (the AI society), a Data Science Club, ACM with a Systems Programming subgroup, Cyberbirds, Game Dev Society and WiCS [JHU-S20].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: About 80% of students are involved in one or more student organization, but no full student-activities directory was fetched to verify breadth [JHU-S27].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: 25% of men and 21% of women join Greek organizations per the 2025-26 CDS, and the two-year residency requirement keeps underclass housing outside Greek control [JHU-S25][JHU-S26].
score_notes.campus_engagement: 93% of first-year students live on campus but only 46% of all undergraduates do, so most juniors and seniors live in surrounding neighborhoods [JHU-S25].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: The O'Connor Center is free to all Homewood students and includes a six-lane pool, climbing wall and bouldering cave, indoor track and three weight rooms, though it closes 3-4 weeks a year for maintenance [JHU-S29][JHU-S31].
score_notes.daily_life: A single contiguous Homewood campus with a two-year residency requirement, on-campus rec center at the North Gate, and off-campus housing within walking distance [JHU-S43][JHU-S28].

robotics_ai.capstone: EN.520.498 and EN.520.499 Capstone Design Project I and II (3 credits each), team-based system engineering evaluated against design criteria, with interdisciplinary participation from BME, ME and CS majors strongly encouraged; ECE also runs multi-semester Ideation and Design Labs (EN.520.151/251/363/463) and EN.520.468 Electronics Design Lab, whose projects may involve 'sensors/actuators, mixed-signal electronics, embedded microcomputers, algorithms, and robotics systems design' (JHU-E1).

door.how_you_enter: There is no ECE admission door: 'When you applied to Hopkins, you applied to the full university, and not to a specific school or major (except in the case of biomedical engineering)' and 'You are not bound to the major you listed on your application' (JHU-E2).
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Identical door by policy. JHU admits university-wide and Biomedical Engineering is the only major with its own admission decision, so ECE and CS applicants receive the same admission review and either can declare after matriculating (JHU-E2).
door.internal_gate: No published GPA or capacity gate to declare Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering; students may choose any major across Krieger and Whiting after matriculation (JHU-E2). The LCSR Robotics Minor requires grades of C- or higher, a minimum of 6 courses and 18 credits, with at least 6 credits outside the primary major department (JHU-E3).

ece.vs_cs: Johns Hopkins is the batch's cleanest 'no separate door' case in the applicant's favor: admission is university-wide with BME as the sole direct-admit exception, so ECE is neither easier nor harder than CS — you get in and then choose. That makes the decision purely about content, and ECE is strong here: EN.520.353/454 control systems, EN.520.241 mechatronics (teams design, build and demonstrate a robotic system), EN.520.465 Machine Perception, EN.520.438 Deep Learning, plus a two-semester capstone. The multiplier is the Laboratory for Computational Sensing and Robotics: its Robotics Minor is 'not owned by any one department' and 'Any student from any department within the university can work toward the minor', so an ECE major can add a transcript-recognized robotics credential built on kinematics/dynamics, systems-and-control and computation-and-sensing.
ece.notable: Whiting's accreditation page lists Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering as separately EAC-accredited BS programs, while Computer Science is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission (JHU-E4). The robotics minor requires at least 6 of the 18 credits outside the student's primary major department, so it forces ECE students into robotics coursework beyond their home department (JHU-E3). EN.620.745 Seminar in Computational Sensing and Robotics is cross-listed into the ECE catalog (JHU-E1).

Direct admits must pass a 45-credit review: C- or better in CMSC131/132 (or 141/142) and MATH140, plus a 2.0 GPA. Internal transfer needs B- grades, a 3.0 GPA and a selective review. Internal transfer is described as extremely limited (about 100 per year, external and internal combined). CS has four specializations: Cybersecurity, Data Science, Machine Learning and Quantum Information. None is a robotics specialization. The CS major's upper-level area lists include no robotics course. CMSC477 is open only to students in the Robotics and Autonomous Systems minor. CS has no controls or hardware courses, so robotics depth here comes mainly from the minor. A student who misses direct admission to CS is unlikely to transfer in later.

door.how_you_enter: Two steps: you apply to and are admitted directly to the A. James Clark School of Engineering, which is itself a Limited Enrollment Program, and then you must clear the Clark School gateway review at 45 credits to continue in an engineering major such as ECE — 'All students accepted directly as freshman into the Clark School of Engineering must complete a series of gateway courses and a review at 45 credits.'
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Maryland runs ECE and CS under two different Limited Enrollment Programs with different severities, and the published requirements differ sharply. The Clark School engineering LEP gateway for newly admitted freshmen requires, by the semester they reach their 45th UMD credit: ENGL 101; ENES 100 (C-); MATH 141 (C- or AP); PHYS 161 (C- or AP); CHEM 135/271/134 (C- or AP); one Distributive Studies Gen-Ed; and a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.00, with only one repeat of any single course allowed. Computer Science is a separate LEP whose published gateway standard is materially higher — the CS minor gateway effective spring 2025 requires CMSC131/133/141 at B-, CMSC132/142 at B-, MATH140 at B- and a 3.0 UMD GPA. A 2.00 continuation GPA for engineering versus B- course grades and a 3.0 GPA for the CS side is the published gap.
door.internal_gate: Clark School LEP gateway review at 45 credits (courses and 2.00 cumulative GPA above, one repeat maximum per course). Beyond that, ECE imposes a course-level control: 'Departmental permission is required in order for students to register and for all courses in the major.' The BSEE also requires a grade of C- or higher in all engineering, mathematics and science courses and their prerequisites. No separate ECE-specific admission gate beyond the Clark School LEP was found on the pages fetched.

ece.vs_cs: At Maryland the whole Clark School is one Limited Enrollment Program, so ECE inherits an engineering-wide gateway (2.00 cumulative GPA plus five specified courses at C- by 45 credits) rather than a department-specific competition, while Computer Science is a separate and stiffer LEP whose published gateway standards run to B- course grades and a 3.0 GPA. ECE gives you a full controls stack (ENEE460/461/463/469), a dedicated ENEE467 Robotics Project Laboratory, ENEE436 Foundations of Machine Learning and ENEE408 Capstone Design — arguably a more complete robotics path than CS at this school. The cost is the absence of a named robotics concentration in the BSEE and the department's requirement that you get departmental permission to register for major courses.
ece.notable: Maryland ECE offers a distinct Cyber-Physical Systems Engineering BS, separately EAC-accredited, whose junior/senior sequence includes ENEB346 Linear Algebra for Machine Learning Applications and ENEB408A/B Capstone Design I/II — this is effectively a purpose-built embedded/autonomy degree and is unusual among the schools in this batch. ECE also offers a Quantum Science and Engineering minor and an ECE Honors Program (honors students may apply up to 6 ENEE499/499L credits versus 5 for others).

door.how_you_enter: You apply to the University of Michigan / College of Engineering, enter undeclared, and then declare: 'Undergraduate students apply to the University of Michigan for admission. Once admitted as a student and maintaining an appropriate academic record, you may declare a major in electrical engineering or computer engineering after talking with an advisor' (UMICH-E2).
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Published policy difference rather than admit rates: Michigan requires CS applicants to be selected into the major at the application stage — 'students who apply for admission into the College of LSA or the College of Engineering and are considering computer science as a major must now request selection into the major on the Common Application' (UMICH-E3) — while the CSE department states 'Students are not required to request advance selection for the computer engineering and data science major programs' (UMICH-E5). Per-major admit rates are not published.
door.internal_gate: First-years enter the College of Engineering undeclared and are urged to declare by the start of their third term; declaring EE or Computer Engineering requires only 'maintaining an appropriate academic record' plus an advisor conversation, with no published GPA threshold or capacity cap (UMICH-E2).

ece.vs_cs: Michigan is the batch's strongest example of ECE being a genuinely less-gated door: EE and Computer Engineering are declared after enrollment with no advance selection, whereas CS applicants must request selection into the major on the Common Application and can be admitted to Michigan without getting CS. The ECE division's own course set is unusually deep in robotics — EECS 367 Intro to Autonomous Robotics, 464 Hands-on Robotics, 465 Algorithmic Robotics, 467 Autonomous Robotics Design Experience, 568 Mobile Robotics, plus 360/461 controls and 442/445 vision and ML. The trade is that CS in Engineering is not ABET-accredited by EAC anyway, so choosing EE or CompE also buys you EAC accreditation that the CS B.S.E. does not carry.
ece.notable: EE and CS live in one EECS department split into an ECE Division and a CSE Division, so ECE students sit inside the same department as CS. The College of Engineering bulletin lists Computer Engineering and Electrical Engineering as EAC-accredited while the B.S.E. in Computer Science is not EAC-accredited (UMICH-E1). Computer Engineering and Data Science are the CSE-side programs that do not require advance selection (UMICH-E5).

name: University of Michigan-Dearborn
undergrad_enrollment_note: UM-Dearborn Facts and Figures lists 6,238 undergraduates (7,741 total students) for AY 2026-27. The Fall 2025 official headcount was 6,199 undergraduates of 8,005 total, per UM-Dearborn News and the U-M Office of Budget and Planning [DBN-C1][DBN-C2][DBN-C3].
degree_name: Bachelor of Science in Engineering in Robotics Engineering (ABET EAC-accredited primary major)
degree_type: Dedicated primary robotics engineering bachelor's degree, 125 credit hours, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering [DBN-R1][DBN-R2]
major_access_full: First-year applicants apply to UM-Dearborn and can be admitted directly into their chosen College of Engineering and Computer Science (CECS) major, including Robotics Engineering; there is no pre-engineering stage. Students without Pre-Calculus credit or a Calculus I placement enter the Dearborn Engineering Success program and must pass MATH 105 or MATH 101 with C- or better within three semesters (excluding summer) while keeping a 2.0 GPA. No separate GPA gate to remain in Robotics Engineering is published [DBN-R13][DBN-R15].
recommended_major_route: Apply with Robotics Engineering (BSE) as the intended major for direct entry. Use the required manipulation, mobile robots, industrial robots, controls and embedded core, then spend the professional/approved elective credits on ECE 434 Machine Learning, ECE/CIS 479 Artificial Intelligence or ECE 4881 Robot Vision [DBN-R1].
alternative_route: BSE Computer Engineering or BSE Electrical Engineering with robotics electives (ECE 3641, 4641, 4881); BS Computer and Information Science with the Artificial Intelligence concentration for a software/AI focus [DBN-R18][DBN-R19][DBN-R20].
primary_structural_risk: Small program (31 students enrolled Fall 2025; 5–10 degrees a year) and a tightly prescribed 125-credit plan with only 7 credits of professional/approved electives. Upper-level robotics and AI electives may not run every term; offering frequency is not published [DBN-R1][DBN-R16].
notable_ai_institute: Institute for Advanced Vehicle Systems (IAVS): applied vehicle-systems research; its Driving Simulator Lab is building scenarios for autonomous driving research and studies human-machine interaction [DBN-R5]. ECE research labs include the Robotic Motion Intelligence (RMI) Lab and the Bio-Inspired Machine Intelligence (BIMI) Lab [DBN-R3].
notable_undergraduate_research_program: SURE (Summer Undergraduate Research Experience): 12 weeks with a faculty mentor, paid $17/hour for up to 15 hours/week; 18 of the 46 SURE 2026 projects were in CECS. Summer 2027 applications open November 2026 [DBN-R22][DBN-R23].
fourplusone_name: Robotics Engineering 4+1 (accelerated BSE/MSE in Robotics Engineering); separate EE/CE and CIS 4+1 options also exist [DBN-R9][DBN-R20]
cost_note: 2026-27 full-time first-year budget, living off campus, is $55,103 for a non-resident: tuition $35,512, fees $400, food and housing $13,890, books $1,300, transportation $2,284, personal $1,717. The Michigan-resident budget is $36,455. UM-Dearborn has no university-owned housing, so the budget uses off-campus living (living-at-home budgets: $26,864 resident, $45,512 non-resident). An NC resident pays the non-resident rate; the Great Lakes in-state-rate award does not cover NC. The 2026-27 fee schedule sets full-time block tuition at $17,556 per term non-resident ($8,232 resident) plus a $200 per-term registration assessment, so the printed $35,512 tuition line already equals tuition plus registration and the separate $400 fee line may be counted twice. The off-campus tuition cell is printed as $35,521; the total matches $35,512. First-year courses carry no college premium. CECS 300-499 level courses add $125 per credit; the 2026-27 upper-division CECS non-resident off-campus budget is $54,998 (tuition $38,112, with a lower $11,330 food and housing line). The Undergrad Non-Resident Scholarship ($5,000-$12,500/yr by GPA) reduces the bill. Federal loan fees are added if loans are accepted.
housing_guarantee: No housing guarantee or residency requirement: UM-Dearborn states it 'does not offer university-owned housing' and points students to private apartments through its Off-Campus Housing Marketplace. The nearest purpose-built option, The Union at Dearborn (780 Town Center Dr, across Evergreen Road), is privately owned and operated, with furnished 2- to 4-bedroom units on 9- or 12-month individual leases [DBN-C4][DBN-C5][DBN-C7]
greek_participation: No participation percentage published on the pages fetched; the Office of Student Life names five fraternities and five sororities. The CDS 2024-25 F1 values could not be read in this session [DBN-C8]
sports_influence: Minor (NAIA; nine varsity teams, eight in the Wolverine-Hoosier Athletic Conference; men's ice hockey in the ACHA Division I GLCHL; no varsity football listed) [DBN-C10][DBN-C11]
recreation_center: Wellness Center (athletics department) — open to current students with UMID, Mon–Fri 7 a.m.–8 p.m., closed Sat–Sun; cardio and free weights to 100 lb, Cybex machines, two lifting platforms, racquetball court, dance studio, golf simulator, fitness classes; no pool listed. The Fieldhouse/Ice Arena at the south end of campus is the varsity venue [DBN-C12][DBN-C10][DBN-C13]

score_notes.cs_foundations: RE requires ECE 270 Computer Methods in ECE I, ECE 370 Advanced Software Techniques in Computer Engineering, ECE 273 Digital Systems and ECE/MATH 276 Discrete Math. No data structures and algorithms course (CIS 350) is required.
score_notes.math_foundations: RE requires MATH 115, 116 and 215 (Calculus I–III), MATH 228 Differential Equations with Linear Algebra, IMSE 317 Engineering Probability and Statistics and discrete math. Linear algebra is combined with differential equations in one 4-credit course.
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: The RE elective lists include ECE 434 Machine Learning, ECE/CIS 479 AI, ECE 4881 Robot Vision and IMSE 489 Robotics Systems Simulation. Campus-wide, CIS also offers Deep Learning, Computational Learning, NLP and Trustworthy AI, and ECE offers ECE 488 Machine Vision.
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: RE leaves only 7 credits of professional and approved electives, so a student fits about two AI/vision courses. No AI course is required in the robotics degree.
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: Deep learning, NLP and trustworthy AI are taught in the CIS AI concentration (CIS 483, 411, 482) but are not on the Robotics Engineering elective lists. Within RE the options are ML, classical AI and robot vision.
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: The 125-credit RE plan is almost fully prescribed, with 3–4 professional plus 3–4 approved elective credits (minimum 7). The Mechatronics and Robotics certificate and 4+1 courses can overlap with the degree.
score_notes.course_availability: The catalog does not publish offering frequency, and the program is small (31 enrolled Fall 2025). No basis to score rotation or seats.
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: SURE pays $17/hour for up to 15 hours/week over 12 weeks, and 18 of 46 SURE 2026 projects were in CECS. ENGR 492 directed research and ECE 491 count as RE electives; lab access needs a faculty sponsor and safety training.
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: A small major (31 students, 5–10 graduates a year) and the two-semester ECE 4987/4988 design sequence give regular faculty contact. SURE pairs each student with a faculty mentor, and the ISC robotics teams have an ECE faculty adviser.
score_notes.project_based_learning: ENGR 100 Introduction to Engineering Design in year one, required lab-based robotics courses, and the two-semester ECE 4987/4988 Robotics Engineering Design sequence. ISC autonomous snowplow and lawn mower teams add competition projects.
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: Required ECE 3641 Robotic Manipulation, ECE 4641 Mobile Robots, IMSE 381 Industrial Robots, ECE 460/ME 442 controls, ECE 3731 embedded systems and ECE 347 Applied Dynamics in an EAC-accredited primary degree. Vision and AI are electives only.
score_notes.computing_resources: No public GPU inventory or undergraduate cluster-access policy was found in the reviewed CECS pages.
score_notes.industry_preparation: The optional ENGR 299/399/499 co-op/internship pathway gives letter-graded credit (up to 3 credits toward electives), and the program page names NASA and Ford among recent employers. No robotics-specific placement data or mandatory co-op was found.
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: SURE, ENGR 492 honors directed research and the RE 4+1 MSE provide research preparation. The program publishes no graduate-school placement figures.
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: Dedicated RE 4+1: up to 9 double-counted 500-level credits, 3.2 CGPA and 60 credits to apply, then 15–21 graduate credits to finish the 30-credit MSE in Robotics Engineering, possibly within three terms after the BSE.
score_notes.intellectual_energy: No retention figure, student-workload accounts or other academic-climate evidence was retrieved in this session; not scored.
score_notes.healthy_ambition: No evidence on grading policy, curve practice or student competitiveness was retrieved in this session; not scored.
score_notes.student_agency: More than 180 registered student organizations with self-service listing through VictorsLink, and CECS lists over 20 clubs and teams, including two student-run Formula SAE teams [DBN-C9][DBN-C14].
score_notes.community_within_scale: About 6,200 undergraduates, but UM-Dearborn offers no university-owned housing, no first-year housing guarantee and no published living-learning community; 93% of undergraduates are Michigan residents [DBN-C1][DBN-C4].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: CECS lists over 20 clubs, teams and professional societies, including Formula SAE Combustion and Electric, an Intelligent Systems Club, an AI Club and MASA; no dedicated robotics competition team is named on that page [DBN-C14].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: The Office of Student Life lists more than 180 organizations across seven categories (hobbies and recreation, civic engagement, cultural, academic, Greek, professional, wellness), plus seven club sports and intramurals [DBN-C9][DBN-C10].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Ten Greek chapters are named, but no participation rate or evidence on evening and weekend social programming was retrieved; not scored [DBN-C8].
score_notes.campus_engagement: With no university-owned housing, the Office of Student Life and Wellness Center closed on weekends and no Sunday shuttle service, published structures for evening and weekend campus activity are limited [DBN-C4][DBN-C9][DBN-C12][DBN-C15].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: The Wellness Center has cardio, weights, a racquetball court, dance studio and golf simulator, but posted hours are weekdays 7 a.m.–8 p.m. only and no pool is listed [DBN-C12].
score_notes.daily_life: Campus is about 20 minutes from DTW and a mile from the Dingell Transit Center; campus shuttles serve nearby apartments until 10 p.m. Mon–Thu and run a Saturday grocery trip, with no Sunday service [DBN-C16][DBN-C15].

best_fit_reason: The BSE requires Robotic Manipulation, Mobile Robots, Industrial Robots, Automatic Control Systems (or ME 442), Microprocessors and Embedded Systems, Applied Dynamics, signals and electronics, plus the two-semester ECE 4987/4988 Robotics Engineering Design sequence. It is EAC-accredited and has a dedicated 4+1 MSE in Robotics Engineering.
biggest_concern: AI depth is limited to roughly two elective courses inside the robotics degree, and the program is small (31 enrolled in Fall 2025), so elective rotation and peer cohort are thin. Deep learning and NLP sit in the CIS AI concentration and are not on the Robotics Engineering elective lists.
evidence_confidence: Official catalog, admissions, aid, Common Data Set and campus sources reviewed October 16, 2026; recommendations and 1–5 scores are analyst assessments. Items still unconfirmed are noted per field.
distance_from_rdu: ~11-12h drive (~678 road miles, routing estimate) / ~2h nonstop RDU-DTW, then ~20 min to campus
verification_note: Reviewed against current official university sources on October 16, 2026.

admissions.overall_admit_rate_note: Fall 2024: 14,105 applied / 7,844 admitted / 1,114 enrolled (CDS 2024-25 C1). Enrolled count is consistent with UM-Dearborn's Fall 2025 report of 1,138 first-year students, 'up 2%'. CollegeData's profile shows the same 14,105 applicants but 7,758 admits.
admissions.admit_rate_note: Institution-level rate for the Fall 2024 first-year cohort. Not a Robotics Engineering rate, a residency-specific rate or an individual probability. No 2025-26 CDS was found on umdearborn.edu as of 2026-10-16.
admissions.admit_rate_note_note: UM-Dearborn's CDS does not publish an in-state vs out-of-state admit split.
admissions.major_admit_context: University admission with an intended major; no separate competitive gate for CECS or Robotics Engineering was found for first-years. Published criteria are GPA-based: 3.00+ guaranteed admission (conduct review applies), 2.75-2.99 potentially admissible, below 2.75 likely not admissible as a first-year. Recommended route: BSE in Robotics Engineering (ABET EAC-accredited). University-wide rates are not major-specific admission probabilities.
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: No Early Decision plan. Admission is rolling.
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: No Early Action plan. Admission is rolling, with decisions released from October 15.
admissions.sat_mid50_note: CDS 2024-25 C9 composite 25th-75th percentile for enrolled Fall 2024 first-years. Section ranges on CollegeData (EBRW 500-620, Math 490-630) sum to the same 990-1250.
admissions.act_mid50_note: CDS 2024-25 C9 ACT composite 25th-75th percentile; CollegeData shows the same 24-29.
admissions.pct_submitting_sat_note: Share of enrolled students submitting SAT could not be read: the CDS PDF stores values in form fields that did not extract, and CollegeData lists it as not reported. Ask UM-Dearborn Institutional Research and Effectiveness.
admissions.pct_submitting_act_note: Not confirmed for the same reason as the SAT share.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS 2024-25 C12 average high-school GPA 3.64 (enrolled Fall 2024 first-years; weighting not stated). The university's Facts and Figures page lists an average incoming first-year GPA of 3.66 (year not stated) and its Fall 2025 enrollment report gives 3.7. Admission decisions use the GPA at the time of admission, usually after junior year.
admissions.test_policy_note: UM-Dearborn's first-year page, which lists the 2027-2028 FAFSA and so covers Fall 2027 entry, states that SAT or ACT scores are optional. The 2026-27 catalog says students can opt in to submit a score (SAT code 1861, ACT code 2074). The Common App profile lists 'Test Optional/Flexible' and says self-reported scores are accepted. CECS notes that ACT scores are considered for its first-year scholarships.
admissions.c7_factors_note: CDS 2024-25 C7 grid; CollegeData's selection-factor list matches it and also lists state residency and geographic residence as not considered. Essays and recommendations are not part of the standard application but may be requested from applicants with a 2.75-2.99 GPA.
admissions.demonstrated_interest_note: CDS C7 marks level of applicant's interest 'not considered'.

interview.mechanism: No admissions interview. CDS C7 marks Interview 'Not Considered'. Applicants can contact an assigned admissions counselor (313-593-5300) or schedule a campus visit; these are informational only.

first_frc_scholarship.application_mechanism: No FIRST/FRC scholarship is listed on UM-Dearborn's first-year scholarship, More First-Year Scholarships, CECS scholarship or Robotics Engineering pages. Incoming CECS students are automatically considered for CECS scholarships with no separate application, based on grades and ACT scores; general merit tiers are also automatic on admission.
first_frc_scholarship.note: CECS states that 2025-26 CECS scholarships were fully awarded and that next-year information would be posted in Spring 2026; amounts are not published. Ask CECS Advising or the One-Stop (313-593-5300) whether FRC participation is weighed in CECS awards.

decision_dates.notification_note: Rolling admission. Decisions are released from October 15 and then on a rolling basis for completed applications. Window labels have null ISO dates.
decision_dates.rd_notify: Rolling; decisions released from October 15, 2026, typically a few weeks after the file is complete
decision_dates.deposit_deadline: Recommended Decision Day May 1, 2027; final commit date for Fall 2027 not yet posted ($50 non-refundable enrollment deposit, hardship waiver available).
decision_dates.restrictions: No ED or EA; single rolling first-year round. Application opens August 1; all transcripts and any test scores must arrive by the deadline. The Common App profile says applying by December 1 is encouraged, and the Robotics Engineering page says earlier applicants may get priority consideration for aid and scholarships. Merit scholarships are automatic on admission.

admissions.decision_dates_note: UM-Dearborn's timeline page shows the 2027-2028 FAFSA (Fall 2027 entry) but still lists 'first day of classes August 26' and final Decision Day August 26, which match the Fall 2026 calendar. The registrar's 2027-2028 calendar shows Fall 2027 classes begin Monday, August 30, 2027, so the final commit date will likely move.
admissions.supplemental_essays_note: No essay or school-specific prompt is required (Common App profile: 'No personal essay required - First Year'). Essays and/or letters of recommendation may be requested after review, mainly for applicants with a 2.75-2.99 GPA.
why_us_ammunition: BSE in Robotics Engineering accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, housed in the Electrical and Computer Engineering department of CECS.

Major core includes ECE 3641 Robotic Manipulation and ECE 4641 Mobile Robots, with ENGR 100 Introduction to Engineering and Engineering Design in the first year; a Robotics Engineering 4+1 path leads to a master's for students holding a 3.2 GPA.
admissions.cs_gate_basis: "All student applicants must meet the criteria for admission to UM-Dearborn" (CECS admission page). No separate first-year CECS gate; the 2.75 GPA and Calculus II rule applies only to current UM-Dearborn students transferring into CECS from another college.
admissions.unit_admit_note: No CECS, Robotics Engineering or residency-specific admission rates are published.

admission_structure.applies_to_note: First-years apply to UM-Dearborn with an intended major; CECS uses the university admission criteria.

admission_structure.internal_mobility: Intended major can be changed before enrollment with the Admission Information Change Form. Current students from other UM-Dearborn colleges entering CECS need a 2.75 cumulative GPA, Calculus II (MATH 116) with C or better, a declared CECS major and a Change of Degree form.

engineering.basis: Recommended engineering route: UM-Dearborn admits first-years to the university with an intended major. CECS states that all student applicants must meet the criteria for admission to UM-Dearborn; no separate first-year CECS or Robotics Engineering admission criterion appears in the 2026-27 catalog or on CECS pages. The catalog recommends two years of algebra, one year of geometry, at least one semester of trigonometry, one year of chemistry and one year of physics or biology for engineering and computer science applicants; students without them may still be admitted and must establish proficiency in the first year.
engineering.how_you_enter: Apply to UM-Dearborn (free UM-Dearborn application or Common App) and list Robotics Engineering (BSE) as the intended major. A 3.0+ high-school GPA is listed as guaranteed admission; 2.75-2.99 is 'potentially admissible' with possible essay/recommendation requests. Most new students take the Mathematics Placement Examination before orientation. Current UM-Dearborn students moving into CECS from another college need a 2.75 cumulative GPA, Calculus II (MATH 116) with C or better and a declared CECS major.

computing.basis: Computing alternative: CS and related CECS majors use the same university admission criteria and catalog math/science recommendations; no separate first-year gate published. Internal transfer into CECS from another college requires a 2.75 GPA and Calculus II.
computing.how_you_enter: Apply to UM-Dearborn and list the CECS computing major as the intended major.

door.easier_than_cs_basis: EE, CE, Robotics Engineering and CIS share the same direct-to-major first-year route and UM-Dearborn publishes no per-major admit rates (DBN-R13, DBN-R15).
door.internal_gate: Students without Pre-Calculus credit or a Calculus I placement enter Dearborn Engineering Success and must pass MATH 105 or MATH 101 with C- or better within three semesters (excluding summer) and hold a 2.0 GPA. The 4+1 option needs a 3.2 cumulative GPA.

ece.vs_cs: UM-Dearborn already has an EAC-accredited Robotics Engineering BSE, so ECE is the hardware-depth alternative rather than the robotics door. EE adds communications, DSP and controls; CE adds architecture, operating systems and embedded design. Both can take ECE 3641, 4641 and 4881 as electives but do not require them. CIS trades hardware for algorithms and offers a dedicated AI concentration with deep learning and NLP.
ece.notable: A dual BSE in Electrical and Computer Engineering takes 141 credits, 16 more than one degree. The ECE department lists 14 teaching labs and 4 research labs, including the Robotics Engineering Laboratory, RMI Lab and BIMI Lab. EE and CE share the 4+1 rules with Robotics Engineering (up to 9 double-counted credits, 3.2 GPA).

score_notes.cs_foundations: Programming and software foundations are assessed in the recommended BS Electrical Engineering — Controls and Robotics Concentration (EFY then CODA) plan. This is not the former CS/AI major; use the home-department core and the prerequisites on Robotics routes.
score_notes.math_foundations: Check calculus, linear algebra, probability and differential-equation preparation against the recommended engineering plan and the controls/learning prerequisites. Do not substitute the former CS/AI major requirements.
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: Supporting options for the recommended route: ECE441 Robot Motion Planning; ECE411 Introduction to Machine Learning; ECE425 Neural Networks and Deep Learning. Prerequisites, permissions and degree credit restrictions are recorded on Robotics routes.
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Supporting AI is elective depth within BS Electrical Engineering — Controls and Robotics Concentration (EFY then CODA). ECE441 Robot Motion Planning; ECE411 Introduction to Machine Learning; ECE425 Neural Networks and Deep Learning. Check the stated prerequisites, permissions and degree-credit rules; these courses are not all required or guaranteed.
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: The reviewed undergraduate options emphasize perception, machine learning and planning for robotics. Graduate institute topics or an alternative AI-major core are not counted as required coursework.
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: The recommended route has its own degree requirements, elective slots and minor-overlap rules. Confirm that each AI or robotics elective counts toward this specific degree; university-wide availability is insufficient.
score_notes.course_availability: Future course offerings, seats and permissions are not guaranteed; current catalogue listings and published annual/every-other-year categories are recorded separately.
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: CSC 299 exists specifically for first- and second-year undergraduate research and the department runs faculty Lightning Talks the first Friday of each semester, though OUR funding caps at $500 supplies + $1,000 of work [NCSU-S13][NCSU-S11].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: Named faculty coordinators for each elective track and honors program plus a recurring department-run mentor-matching event [NCSU-S15][NCSU-S14][NCSU-S13].
score_notes.project_based_learning: Home-department design/capstone and documented robotics course projects support this route. College of Engineering Robotics Initiative; ARoS laboratory accepts NC State student-volunteer applications; student teams include BattlePack, RoboPack and AquaPack. Legacy CRIM URLs now return HTTP410; planned robotics minor is not yet a verified catalog offering. A robotics lab or industry sponsor does not guarantee an undergraduate position.
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: Joint NC State / UNC Asheville B.S. in Engineering (EAC); 9 undergrad robotics courses. 6 labs, CRIM, 2 competition teams.
score_notes.computing_resources: No page documenting undergraduate GPU or HPC cluster access was retrieved this session.
score_notes.industry_preparation: General programme preparation context; CS salaries, company bands and graduate institute research are not verified robotics-major placement outcomes. Confirm the selected degree’s graduate option and any eligible co-op/research pathway.
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: General programme preparation context; CS salaries, company bands and graduate institute research are not verified robotics-major placement outcomes. Confirm the selected degree’s graduate option and any eligible co-op/research pathway.

score_notes.intellectual_energy: Hack_NCState drew a 24-hour, free, cross-disciplinary field into Talley's State Ballroom in February 2026 and HackPack ran a CTF in April 2026 [NCSU-S22a][NCSU-S23].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: Major grade rules are permissive (C/C- minimums, 2.0 major-GPA floor), but CODA forces first-year competition for capacity-limited CS seats judged on chemistry, physics and calculus grades [NCSU-S1][NCSU-S4].
score_notes.student_agency: CSC 299/490/499 proposals, three concentrations and three elective tracks give real choice, yet graduate courses are restricted to Honors/ABM students and AI students are barred from the Robotics Track [NCSU-S13][NCSU-S15].
score_notes.community_within_scale: CSC Honors, ABM, robotics teams and HackPack provide sub-communities inside a College of Engineering of more than 12,500 students; the living-learning village roster was not retrievable [NCSU-S27][NCSU-S33].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: Four separate technical organizations have dated 2025-26 activity: Hack_NCState (Feb 14-15, 2026), HackPack CTF (Apr 17-18, 2026), Aerial Robotics Club (2025-26 NC Space Grant award) and RoboPack [NCSU-S22a][NCSU-S23][NCSU-S25b][NCSU-S25c].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: No student-organization directory or event calendar was fetched this session.
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Official FSL data updated Summer 2026 shows 52 chapters and 3,800+ members at "more than 15%" of undergraduates, with Greek Village housing only 767 residents, so roughly 85% are unaffiliated and Greek life does not control housing [NCSU-S34].
score_notes.campus_engagement: No evidence was gathered on weekend/evening campus life, traditions, or residential versus commuter patterns.
score_notes.recreation_facilities: 430,000 sq ft across the Wellness and Recreation Center and Carmichael Gym with 11 indoor courts, an Olympic weightlifting room, the Casey Aquatic Center, a Climbing Center and an indoor track, included automatically in student fees [NCSU-S37][NCSU-S38].

admissions.admit_rate_note: IN-STATE vs OUT-OF-STATE (Fall 2024, CDS): North Carolina residents 21,636 applied / 10,570 admitted = 48.9%. Out-of-state 19,487 applied / 6,963 admitted = 35.7%. International 2,920 applied / 668 admitted = 22.9%. The in-state advantage is roughly 13 percentage points, and it is policy-driven: UNC System Policy 700.1.3 caps nonresidents at 18 percent of NC State's fall first-time undergraduate class, with a State operating budget reduction if the cap is exceeded for two consecutive fiscal years.

admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: NC State offers no Early Decision plan (CDS C21 = No).
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 confirms a non-binding Early Action plan closing November 1 with notification January 30, but NC State publishes no EA application or admit counts. NC State does say 'We don't necessarily give priority to early action applicants in the review process, but first-year early action applicants receive priority consideration for scholarships and financial aid' [NCSU-S2].
admissions.sat_mid50_note: Fall 2024 CDS C9: composite 25th 1290 / 50th 1360 / 75th 1440, from 1,422 enrolled submitters.
admissions.act_mid50_note: ACT composite 25th 25 / 50th 29 / 75th 32, from 2,365 enrolled submitters (41.34%) — NC State is one of the few schools in this set where ACT submission exceeds SAT submission.
admissions.pct_submitting_sat_note: 24.86% of enrolled first-years submitted SAT scores; 41.34% submitted ACT scores.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS C12 average high school GPA 3.83, reported for 98% of enrolled first-years; CDS C11 shows 20.02% with a 4.0 GPA and CDS C10 shows 40% in the top tenth of their class. The College of Engineering states the typical admitted first-year has an unweighted GPA of 3.8-4.0.
admissions.test_policy_note: Conditional test-optional with a GPA floor. CDS C8 states verbatim: 'We are test optional for applicants with a weighted GPA of 2.8 or above. International students for whom English is not their first language will be required to submit an English proficiency test.' The 2024-25 CDS labels these policies 'for use in admission for Fall 2026', with a latest receipt date of February 1, so Fall 2027 applicability is inferred from the standing UNC System-aligned rule. Applicants below a 2.8 weighted GPA must submit a score.
admissions.c7_note: CDS C7 also marks geographical residence and state residency 'Considered', consistent with the 18 percent nonresident cap.

interview.mechanism: No admissions interview is offered or considered; CDS C7 marks Interview 'Not Considered'. Portfolio review substitutes for studio-based majors (10-piece portfolio plus an additional essay, due November 1).

An FRC applicant should search PackASSIST after admission rather than expect a named FIRST award.

admissions.cs_gate_basis: All engineering first-years enter Engineering First-Year and compete through ranked CODA against per-department seat caps.

admission_structure.applies_to_note: major (engineering applicants are admitted into the Engineering First Year program)
units_named: Up to two majors are selected, each housed in one of the colleges: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, College of Design, College of Education, College of Engineering, College of Humanities and Social Sciences, College of Natural Resources, College of Sciences, Wilson College of Textiles, Poole College of Management, plus University College/Exploratory Studies. Engineering entrants join the 'Engineering First Year Program (EFY)'.
admission_structure.internal_mobility: Post-enrollment major changes are 'on a space available basis'; engineering students move from EFY into a degree major through the college's placement process.

engineering.basis: Recommended engineering route: Engineering First Year admission is not EE admission. CODA ranks qualified applicants for department-set seat capacity;2.0 continuation/CODA GPA guarantees only an available engineering program, not the intended EE or CS major.
engineering.how_you_enter: Two steps: all first-year engineering students are admitted into the Engineering First Year (EFY) program rather than to ECE, then they complete the CODA (Change of Degree Audit) requirements — earliest in December of the first year — to move into Electrical Engineering, EE REES or Computer Engineering. Students in Exploratory Studies or other majors can also take the CODA courses and apply.

computing.basis: Computing alternative: Same as ECE: admitted to Engineering First Year, then apply to Computer Science through CODA after the required first-year courses, competing for a capped number of seats ranked by CODA GPA. Formal transcript concentrations are Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Game Development and Software Engineering; none is robotics. The Robotics Track uses four CSC restricted electives (12 hours): required CSC 495 special topics in robot motion planning and software engineering for robotics plus CSC 422, and one elective (e.g. CSC 453 or CSC 495 Introduction to Mobile Robotics). A 2.5 major GPA earns a completion letter. The track page states AI Concentration students are not eligible for it. The BS CS is ABET CAC (computing), not EAC. 2025-26 combined CODA data: 186 EFY first-choice applicants, 185 taken, CODA GPA middle 50% 3.27-3.87.

door.how_you_enter: Two steps: all first-year engineering students are admitted into the Engineering First Year (EFY) program rather than to ECE, then they complete the CODA (Change of Degree Audit) requirements — earliest in December of the first year — to move into Electrical Engineering, EE REES or Computer Engineering. Students in Exploratory Studies or other majors can also take the CODA courses and apply.
door.easier_than_cs_basis: NC State publishes CODA statistics per major. For 2024-25 overall, Electrical Engineering had 183 first-choice applicants and 176 enrolled, with an EFY middle-50% CODA GPA of 3.22-3.95 and cumulative GPA 3.24-4.01; Computer Engineering had 120 applicants and 112 enrolled with CODA GPA 3.29-3.92; Computer Science had 268 applicants and 259 enrolled with CODA GPA 3.43-3.97. Both EE and CpE therefore show lower matriculant GPA profiles than CS, with CS demand roughly 1.5x EE. Note the caveat: because CODA operates on a guarantee-plus-capacity model rather than a published admit rate, the applicant/enrolled ratios are not admit rates.
door.internal_gate: CODA. The CODA GPA is computed from six Success courses (MA 141, MA 241, PY 205, PY 206, CH 101, CH 102), each of which must be passed with a C or better, and the CODA GPA must be at least 2.0; students must also complete ENG 101, E 101 and E 102 with C- or better and E 115 with an S. Requisites must be completed within four fall/spring semesters. 'Only students in the Engineering First Year program with a CODA GPA greater than or equal 2.0 and a continuation GPA of 2.0 will be guaranteed entrance into at least one of the remaining programs with available seats' — the guarantee is to a program with seats, not to your first choice. Practically, ECE gates course access too: 'Students must CODA into EE, EE REES, or CPE to take 300 courses.'

ece.vs_cs: NC State ECE has the most explicit robotics offering in this batch: a published Controls and Robotics Concentration in the BSEE, 24 hours built on ECE 308 Elements of Control Systems plus a required-elective menu of ECE 441 Robot Motion Planning, ECE 455 Industrial Robotic Systems, ECE 411 Introduction to Machine Learning and ECE 425/525 Neural Networks and Deep Learning, capped by ECE 484/485 Senior Design. As a North Carolina resident the applicant gets in-state consideration at the admission step, but the real gate is CODA after enrollment, and the published statistics show EE matriculants clearing at a lower GPA band (3.22-3.95 CODA GPA) than CS matriculants (3.43-3.97) with far fewer applicants. The cost is a genuine one-year deferral of major identity: you cannot take 300-level ECE courses until you have CODA'd in.
ece.notable: The EE degree also lists an AI & Machine Learning concentration and a Digital Circuits concentration alongside Controls and Robotics. ECE offers an EE/CpE dual degree program reachable through CODA. The earliest an EFY student can CODA is December of the first year, which means a strong fall semester is the whole game.

door.how_you_enter: Direct application to a named major or a combined major: you apply to the College of Engineering for BS Computer Engineering or BS Electrical Engineering, or to an intercollege combined major such as Computer Engineering and Computer Science (College of Engineering plus the Khoury College of Computer Sciences).
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Northeastern does not publish per-major or per-college admit rates on the pages fetched, so no numeric ECE-versus-CS comparison is available. Structurally, the Computer Engineering and Computer Science combined major is an intercollege degree and is 'fully accredited as a Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering and adds the computer science depth', which means it is admitted through the engineering side rather than as a standalone Khoury CS admit.
door.internal_gate: No published GPA or capacity gate to declare or remain in ECE was found on the pages fetched. The combined-major BSCmpE requires 135 total semester hours.

ece.vs_cs: Northeastern's differentiator is not admissions math but the co-op engine: more than 90 percent of ECE undergraduates do co-op, typically two to three six-month placements, and ECE co-op employers include Amazon Robotics, iRobot, Analog Devices, Apple, Draper, MIT Lincoln Laboratory, Tesla and SpaceX, with the College running a dedicated Robotics Week featuring Amazon Robotics, Boston Dynamics, Shield AI, Symbotic and Piaggio Fast Forward. The combined Computer Engineering and Computer Science major is the strongest single answer to the ECE-versus-CS question here because it is one degree that is ABET-accredited as Computer Engineering while adding CS depth (CS 3000, CS 3650, CS 4530 alongside EECE 2160 Embedded Design: Enabling Robotics and the EECE 4791/4792 capstone). The cost is length and load: 135 semester hours plus co-op cycles push the degree toward five calendar years.
ece.notable: Intercollege combined majors pairing engineering with computer science (Computer Engineering and Computer Science) plus Computer Engineering and Physics, Electrical Engineering and Physics, and Electrical Engineering and Music. ECE offers a Minor in Robotics, an MS in Robotics, and a PlusOne accelerated master's pathway; graduate robotics courses EECE 5550 Mobile Robotics, EECE 5552 Assistive Robotics and EECE 5554 Robotics Sensing and Navigation are ECE-taught and reachable through PlusOne.

admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025 (Columbus campus): 81,392 applicants, 40,047 admitted, 8,248 enrolled = 49.2% [OSU-S1]. In-state 11,395/25,273 = 45.1%; out-of-state 19,914/42,898 = 46.4%; international 8,738/13,221 = 66.1% [OSU-S1] (INFERRED - division of CDS C1 counts). Note the pattern: OSU's in-state and out-of-state admit rates are nearly identical, but yield differs sharply - 5,609 of 8,248 enrollees are Ohio residents [OSU-S1]. Waitlist: 5,358 offered, 2,278 accepted a place, 2,049 admitted [OSU-S1] - the only school in this batch where the waitlist is a live path.

admissions.test_detail_note: Fall 2025 enrolled: SAT submitted by 25% (2,099), ACT by 42% (3,474) - the only school in this batch where ACT submission exceeds SAT. SAT composite 25th/50th/75th = 1300/1380/1440; ACT 27/30/32 [OSU-S1].
admissions.gpa_note_detail: OSU leaves CDS C11/C12 blank, so no institution-reported GPA distribution or average is available [OSU-S1]. Class rank instead: 73% top tenth, 96% top quarter, 99% top half, with 27% submitting rank [OSU-S1].
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: REQUIRED - this is a change from prior cycles and the biggest surprise in this batch. CDS C8 states SAT/ACT are 'Required to be considered for admission' for Fall 2027 [OSU-S1], the admissions site confirms 'Yes, standardized test scores from ACT or SAT are required for first-year applicants to the Columbus campus,' superscoring is used, and the last usable test dates for Early Action are October 3 (SAT) / October 17 (ACT) [OSU-S3]; the university announced the reinstatement publicly [OSU-S5]. CDS C8E gives a latest test date of 1/15 and notes scores are used for advising/placement [OSU-S1].
admissions.c7_note: C7 grid visually confirmed from the CDS page image (the PDF text layer omits the checkbox values). Test scores are Very Important here - the only school in this batch to rate them that highly - consistent with the reinstated requirement. Volunteer work and work experience are both Important, unusually high. Alumni relation and religious affiliation Not Considered; geographical residence and state residency Considered [OSU-S1].
