engineering.basis: Recommended engineering route: DIRECT ECE: college memo documents direct first-year admission from Autumn 2023. Fall 2027 policy should be reconfirmed; CSE automatic enrollment language applies explicitly only to 2025-26.

computing.basis: Computing alternative: First-years must choose Computer Science and Engineering (Pre) on the Common App and start as pre-majors. Since Autumn 2025, CSE has moved pre-majors into the major automatically with no extra application, but it says this policy is reviewed each year. No robotics specialization. The closest is the Artificial Intelligence specialization: CSE 3521 required plus two of CSE 5523, 5524, 5525, 5526, 5243 or 5914. Robotics hardware courses (ECE/ME 5463) would come through the Robotics and Autonomous Systems minor. Admission rules are in flux: the college's Admission to Major page still lists CSE as Limited Space, while its newer Request to Enroll page lists only Aerospace, Biomedical and Mechanical as limited-capacity. CSE's admissions page (modified Oct 2025) still says you cannot switch into pre-CSE after being admitted to Ohio State in another major, so CSE must be the major named on the application. A sister option is the BS CIS in Arts and Sciences with the same CS core.

door.how_you_enter: You apply to Ohio State indicating a major; engineering students on the Columbus campus then move into ECE as a 'Space Available Program', which requires only good standing with a 2.0 GPA and no separate major application.
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Published entry-to-major policy differs: ECE is a Space Available Program open to engineering students in good standing with a 2.0 GPA or above 'without the need to submit an admission application', while Computer Science is a Limited Space Program that requires a major application and, per CSE's published mechanism, students 'who have a cumulative GPA of 3.2 or above and have completed the prerequisite courses are admitted to the major' (OSU-E5, OSU-E6). No per-major admit rates are published, so this is a policy-threshold difference rather than a published yield comparison.
door.internal_gate: 2.0 cumulative GPA and good standing in the College of Engineering, no application required (OSU-E5)

ece.vs_cs: Ohio State ECE hands you the physical robot: 73 core credit hours plus 31 hours of ECE electives structured across seven domains, so you can concentrate in Control and still reach across to Computers and Communications/DSP (OSU-E3), with named courses in real-time robotics, feedback control, embedded systems, vehicle autonomy and machine learning for ECE (OSU-E4). CSE gives deeper software, algorithms and AI theory but is enrollment-limited behind a 3.2 GPA gate, whereas ECE admits any engineering student at 2.0 (OSU-E5, OSU-E6). The cost of ECE is a heavier prescribed core with less room for free electives and less software depth.
ece.notable: The Robotics and Autonomous Systems minor requires ECE/ME 5463, so ECE owns the gateway robotics course for the campus-wide minor. Computer engineering BSECE majors take 84 core credit hours plus 20 technical/directed elective hours, a heavier core than the EE program (OSU-E3).

abet.quote: Both the BS programs in Computer Engineering and Electrical Engineering are accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission's General Criteria and Program Criteria for Electrical, Computer, Communications, Telecommunication(s) and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

robotics_ai.concentration_name: Automatic Control; Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning (offered as concentrations in both BSEE and BSCmpE)

courses.title: Digital Control Systems Analysis and Design

robotics_ai.capstone: ECE 47700 Digital Systems Senior Project is listed as the senior project course in the Computer Engineering course area; ECE degree rules also require an overall GPA of at least 2.000 in courses applying to the ECE major area (PURDUE-E1, PURDUE-E2).

door.how_you_enter: Two steps: you first apply to and are admitted to the College of Engineering (46.1% admit rate), entering First-Year Engineering rather than a named major, and then complete First-Year Engineering requirements and go through the Transition to Major (T2M) process to declare ECE, ranking first and second choices.
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Purdue's published freshman profile gives College of Engineering 46.1% and Computer Science 35.9% (Polytechnic Institute 54.2%), so the admission step into the college that contains ECE is more than 10 points more permissive than the direct Computer Science admit. Purdue's T2M pages further list the capacity-limited majors as Aeronautical & Astronautical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Multidisciplinary Engineering and Mechanical Engineering; ECE is not on that list (PURDUE-E3, PURDUE-E4, PURDUE-E5).
door.internal_gate: T2M after First-Year Engineering: complete FYE requirements, then request a major. No published minimum GPA for ECE; FYE advising flags students with cumulative GPA of 2.80 or below only when their first choice is a capacity-limited major (ME, AAE, BME), and ECE is not listed as capacity-limited. The ECE degree itself requires an overall GPA of at least 2.000 in courses applying to the ECE major area.

ece.vs_cs: Purdue ECE gives you a named Automatic Control concentration plus an AI & Machine Learning concentration in either the BSEE or the BSCmpE, so you get feedback control, embedded microprocessor design and robotics coursework (ECE 56900 Introduction to Robotic Systems) inside an EAC-accredited engineering degree. The cost is the First-Year Engineering detour: you cannot declare ECE as an applicant, and you must clear FYE requirements before T2M. Compared with Computer Science, the front door is materially wider (46.1% vs 35.9%) and ECE is not on Purdue's capacity-limited major list, so the second gate is also softer.
ece.notable: ECE lists Quantum Technology and Microelectronics & Semiconductors concentrations alongside AI/ML; ECE prefers CS 15900 as the First-Year Engineering selective, so an ECE-bound student should take the programming selective in FYE. 32 credits of upper-level ECE must be taken at West Lafayette.

ai_electives.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
ai_electives.access_note: Published Computer Engineering course-area option; confirm current cohort degree applicability and prerequisites. The AI/ML concentration is linked officially, but its current catalogue requirements were inaccessible.

cost_note: 2026-27 West Lafayette nonresident CS/Data Science/Engineering full budget is $53,438, including the $4,050 annual program differential. General nonresident budget is $49,388. Robotics Engineering Technology in Polytechnic has separate program fees and must be costed independently.
fit_basis: Qualitative robotics-first curriculum/access assessment for the recommended degree. Separate from admissions difficulty, personal fit, financial aid and historical career metrics.

name: Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology
institution_type: Private, engineering-focused institute with undergraduate and graduate programs
degree_name: BS Computer Engineering + Multidisciplinary Minor in Robotics (CPE track)
degree_type: Engineering BS (EAC-accredited Computer Engineering) with a multidisciplinary robotics minor [ROSE-HULMAN-E4][ROSE-R1]
program_archetype: B (Computer Engineering robotics route), with D (integrated undergraduate projects)
major_access_full: Admission is to Rose-Hulman as a whole; the application pages describe no major-specific admission. Students start in their chosen curriculum in the first year, and undecided students are told to 'commit to a major program of study' in the first fall. Changing majors means notifying the Registrar 'as soon as possible'; the catalog publishes no GPA or capacity gate. [ROSE-HULMAN-E7][ROSE-R23][ROSE-R12]
recommended_major_route: Apply intending Computer Engineering (CPE). Add the robotics minor's CPE track: take ECE 320 instead of ECE 380, plus ME/CSSE 435, ECE 425, CSSE 463 and 8 credits of Robo Electives. Use the CSSE-eligible area elective and free electives for CSSE 461, CSSE 415 or CSSE 416. [ROSE-HULMAN-E4][ROSE-R1]
alternative_route: BS Electrical Engineering + robotics minor (EE track: CSSE 220 plus 8 credits of Robo Electives; ECE 320 is already required), or BS Computer Science + robotics minor (CS track: ME 230 Mechatronic Systems plus 8 credits of Robo Electives) with the AI specialization.
primary_structural_risk: The CPE degree is 194 quarter credits with only 12 area-elective, 4 technical-elective and 8 free-elective credits. The robotics minor's CPE track adds ME/CSSE 435, ECE 425, CSSE 463 and 8 credits of Robo Electives, so AI electives compete for the same few slots. Only 4 CSSE credits count as CPE area electives.
notable_ai_institute: No AI institute. AI teaching sits in the CSSE department: an AI minor open to any major, an AI specialization in the CS major, and an AI major listed on the department site. [ROSE-R11][ROSE-R14][ROSE-R15]
notable_undergraduate_research_program: Rose Research Fellows: paid research cohort for first- and second-year students (MDS 220/221; 18 fellows in 2024-25). Also R-SURF ten-week summer research fellowships and paid student internships at Rose-Hulman Ventures. [ROSE-R16][ROSE-R17][ROSE-R18][ROSE-R19]
fourplusone_name: Rose Squared (R²): concurrent BS + Master of Engineering Management in four years, with plans listed for Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering and Computer Science. Technical ECE master's (MSEE thesis, MECE course-based) exist, but no accelerated CPE-to-ECE master's route is published. [ROSE-R20][ROSE-HULMAN-E2]
housing_guarantee: First-year residence required ('all freshmen are required to live on campus'); no published guarantee for upper years, which the school says 'many' choose to keep. 96.9% of first-years and 55.0% of all undergraduates live in college housing (CDS 2025-26) [RH-S02][RH-S01]
greek_participation: 37% of men, 33% of women (CDS 2025-26, data year 2024-25); among first-years 28% of men, 33% of women; 8 fraternities, 3 sororities, recruitment from early September [RH-S01][RH-S04]
sports_influence: Minor (NCAA Division III, HCAC); 20 varsity sports with 600+ student-athletes as of 2024, more than a quarter of undergraduates [RH-S07][RH-S06]
recreation_center: Sports and Recreation Center (SRC) — Mon–Thu 6 a.m.–midnight, Fri 6 a.m.–10 p.m., Sat 10 a.m.–7 p.m., Sun 6 p.m.–midnight, with 8-lane 25-yard pool, fieldhouse indoor track, weight and cardio rooms and bouldering wall [RH-S05]
best_fit_reason: Computer Engineering gives embedded systems (ECE 230), architecture, operating systems and linear controls (ECE 320 for robotics-minor students). The robotics minor adds Robotics Engineering (ME/CSSE 435), Mobile Robotics (ECE 425) and Image Recognition (CSSE 463). Projects run from the first-year ECE 160 robot competition to a three-term client-driven senior design.
biggest_concern: Robotics is a minor, not a degree, and there are no named robotics research labs. Elective room in the 194-credit CPE plan is tight, so AI depth beyond two or three courses needs careful planning. Robotics research depends on individual faculty and the paid fellowship programs.
evidence_confidence: Official catalog, admissions, aid, Common Data Set and campus sources reviewed October 16, 2026; recommendations and 1–5 scores are analyst assessments. Items still unconfirmed are noted per field.

score_notes.cs_foundations: The CPE plan requires CSSE 120, 220, 230 (Data Structures and Algorithm Analysis), 232 (Computer Architecture I) and 332 (Operating Systems) alongside ECE 230 embedded systems [ROSE-HULMAN-E4].
score_notes.math_foundations: The CPE plan requires MA 111-113, MA 221, MA 222, MA 381 and MA 374 plus a math/science elective. These meet the math prerequisites of CSSE 415/416 and CSSE 461 [ROSE-HULMAN-E4][ROSE-R10].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: The CSSE catalog lists CSSE 286 Intro ML, 313 AI, 314 Bio-Inspired AI, 315 NLP, 415 ML, 416 Deep Learning, 453 Topics in AI, 461 Computer Vision and 463 Image Recognition; most are Robo Electives [ROSE-R10][ROSE-R1].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: CSSE 463 is required in the minor's CPE track, but only 4 CSSE credits count as CPE area electives, so further ML/vision courses must use technical, free or Robo Elective slots. Two or three AI courses is a realistic ceiling in CPE [ROSE-HULMAN-E4][ROSE-R1].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: The AI degrees page lists Generative AI, Deep Reinforcement Learning, AI Safety (CSSE 316) and Designing and Building AI Systems (CSSE 417) among options, but these sit in the AI program rather than the CPE plan [ROSE-R15].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: CPE is 194 quarter credits with 12 area, 4 technical and 8 free elective credits. The robotics minor adds about five courses for CPE; ECE 320 replaces ECE 380 so it adds no length [ROSE-HULMAN-E4][ROSE-R1].
score_notes.course_availability: No current term-by-term offering rotation was found for ME/CSSE 435, ECE 425 or the CSSE AI electives; no score assigned. Ask the robotics program director or ECE advisor for the rotation.
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: Rose Research Fellows give paid research to first- and second-year students (18 fellows in 2024-25), R-SURF funds ten-week summer research, and CSSE says students can start research 'as early as their first year on campus' [ROSE-R16][ROSE-R17][ROSE-R18][ROSE-R27].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: An undergraduate-focused institute where the robotics program lists nine faculty across ME, ECE and CSSE, and Research Fellows work with faculty mentors; no robotics-specific mentoring measure is published [ROSE-R2][ROSE-R16].
score_notes.project_based_learning: ECE 160 ends in a first-year team competition, ECE 230 and ECE 425 have team projects, CSSE 435 programs a mobile robot for a GPS challenge, and ECE 460-462 is a three-quarter client project [ROSE-R3][ROSE-R10].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: The minor's CPE track requires ME/CSSE 435 Robotics Engineering, ECE 425 Mobile Robotics, ECE 320 controls and CSSE 463, with ECE 420, ME 445 and CSSE 461 as Robo Electives. No dedicated robotics degree [ROSE-R1].
score_notes.computing_resources: The CSSE department runs GPU servers (8x GTX 1080 Ti and 10x Quadro RTX 6000) used in CSSE 461 coursework, reachable on the campus network; no published undergraduate research-compute policy [ROSE-R28].
score_notes.industry_preparation: The ECE department reports a 'nearly 100 percent career placement rate', and Rose-Hulman Ventures employs paid student interns on company prototyping projects. Placement figures are department-reported and not robotics-specific [ROSE-HULMAN-E1][ROSE-R19].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: CSSE seniors can take a three-term senior research or thesis option and the department cites alumni in research programs at Princeton, Brown and Carnegie Mellon; the CPE route has a design capstone instead of a thesis [ROSE-R9][ROSE-R27].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: Rose Squared pairs CPE, EE or CS with a Master of Engineering Management in four years, which is a management degree. No accelerated technical ECE or robotics master's route is published, and CPE area electives cannot double-count toward the MSEE [ROSE-R20][ROSE-R21].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: First-to-second-year retention is 91.6% with an 11:1 student-faculty ratio, and 14 innovation-center competition teams posted national or world-level results in 2025-26 [RH-S01][RH-S09].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: No grading-policy or student-culture evidence on competitiveness was retrieved in this session; ask current students how collaborative the 10-week quarters feel.
score_notes.student_agency: Fourteen student-run competition teams in the Branam/Kremer Innovation Centers, a MakerLab, and a robotics club that states 'Previous experience is not required' [RH-S08].
score_notes.community_within_scale: 2,160 undergraduates, required first-year residence with 96.9% of first-years on campus, and two new or renovated first-year halls (MRH 2025, Speed 2026) built around floor lounges and open doors [RH-S01][RH-S02][RH-S03][RH-S22].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: Robotics alone runs Combat, MATE ROV, Thornbots (RoboMaster) and Rover subteams plus VEX U; 2025-26 results include VEX U World Championship qualification, 5th at the ARC Championship and 2nd at National Havoc Robotics League, alongside Rose Aerial Systems, Rocketry and Formula SAE [RH-S08][RH-S09].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: More than 90 clubs including performing arts (Pep Band, Improv, Dance, Drama), religious, service and club sports — solid coverage but a short list next to larger schools [RH-S10][RH-S11].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Greek participation is high (37% of men, 33% of women per CDS) with most fraternities in off-campus houses, and Terre Haute is a city of about 60,000 with no transit noted by the school; a Student Activities Board exists [RH-S01][RH-S04][RH-S12][RH-S10].
score_notes.campus_engagement: Nearly all first-years live on campus and the SRC is open to midnight Mon–Thu, but only 55% of all undergraduates live in college housing, so upper-year life spreads into fraternity houses and off-campus rentals [RH-S01][RH-S05].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: SRC opens at 6 a.m. weekdays and stays open to midnight Mon–Thu, with an 8-lane natatorium, indoor track and bouldering wall; weekend hours and lifeguarded pool times are short [RH-S05].
score_notes.daily_life: Campus sits on US 40 east of Terre Haute; the school lists no public transit, the nearest airline airport is Indianapolis about an hour away, and the main car-free link is the National Road Heritage Trail to downtown [RH-S12][RH-S13][RH-S14].

admissions.overall_admit_rate_note: Fall 2025: 5,991 applied / 4,847 admitted / 484 enrolled (CDS C1). Fall 2024: 6,097 applied / 4,686 admitted (76.9%) / 604 enrolled (2024-25 CDS C1).
admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025 CDS C1 by residency: Indiana 1,341 applied / 967 admitted (72.1%); out-of-state 3,614 / 3,075 (85.1%); international 1,036 / 805 (77.7%). These are different applicant pools; the split does not show an individual residency advantage.
admissions.major_admit_context: Institute-level admission through the GoRose App or Common App; there are no separately admitting colleges and an Undecided Major option exists. No published major-level admission rates. Minimum preparation before enrolling: four years of math, four years of English, three years of lab science (one year each of biology, chemistry and physics) and two years of social sciences; CDS C5 recommends a fifth math unit and a fourth science unit. Changing majors is done by notifying the Registrar; the catalog lists no GPA or capacity limit. Recommended robotics route: B.S. Computer Engineering (or EE/ME) plus the Multidisciplinary Robotics Minor. University-wide rates are not major-specific admission probabilities.
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: No Early Decision plan. Rose-Hulman offers non-binding Early Action (Nov 1) and Regular Decision (Feb 1) only.
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 lists Early Action (closing November 1, notification December 15) but reports no EA application or admit counts. No early-round admission advantage is established.
admissions.sat_mid50_note: Fall 2025 CDS C9: SAT composite 25th 1270 / 50th 1380 / 75th 1450 (mean 1357), from 173 enrolled submitters. EBRW 620-720; Math 650-750.
admissions.act_mid50_note: Fall 2025 CDS C9: ACT composite 25th 28 / 50th 31 / 75th 34, from 80 enrolled submitters. ACT Math 28-34.
admissions.pct_submitting_sat_note: 35.7% of enrolled first-years (173) submitted SAT scores; 16.5% (80) submitted ACT scores (CDS C9).
admissions.pct_submitting_act_note: 16.5% of enrolled first-years (80) submitted ACT scores (CDS C9).
admissions.gpa_note: CDS C12 average high school GPA 3.91, reported for 97.9% of enrolled first-years (474 of 484); scale/weighting not specified. CDS C11: 59.5% at 4.00, 26.2% at 3.75-3.99, 10.3% at 3.50-3.74, 4.0% at 3.00-3.49. CDS C10 (38% submitted rank): 59.2% top tenth, 85.9% top quarter. Do not compare the average directly with a personal weighted GPA.
admissions.test_policy_note: CDS C8 marks SAT/ACT not required (test-optional) for Fall 2027 applicants, with February 1 as the latest score-receipt date. The admission criteria page states Rose-Hulman 'does not require standardized test scores for admission'; applicants who want scores considered self-report them on the application. Common App lists 'Test Optional/Flexible - First Year'. SAT code 1668, ACT code 1232.
admissions.c7_note: Ratings are from the 2025-26 CDS C7 as read in the August 2026 audit. The PDF's checkbox marks do not survive text extraction, so the ratings could not be re-read on 2026-10-16; the factor list and the rest of the CDS were re-checked.

interview.mechanism: No required interview. Domestic students attending high school in the U.S. may submit an optional 60-90 second Glimpse video; Rose-Hulman states that students who do not submit one 'are at no disadvantage in the review process.' International applicants and domestic students attending high school abroad may submit an optional InitialView interview: 'InitialView interviews are not required and applicants without one are at no disadvantage in our review process.' The 2025-26 CDS C7 rates Interview 'Considered'.

first_frc_scholarship.name: FIRST Robotics Scholarship
first_frc_scholarship.amount: Two merit-based awards of $10,000 per year, renewable up to $40,000 over four years.
first_frc_scholarship.renewable: Yes - renewal is contingent on maintaining good academic standing.
first_frc_scholarship.stackable_with_merit: UNPUBLISHED - the scholarship page does not say whether it combines with the automatic Rose-Hulman Merit Scholarship; verify with Financial Aid.
first_frc_scholarship.application_mechanism: Open to high school seniors who have participated on a FIRST team during high school and who meet regular admission requirements. Only admitted students may apply; the application is on the applicant portal under the admit tab. FIRST participation does not award the scholarship automatically. Rose-Hulman also lists a separate VEX Robotics Scholarship ($10,000, renewable to $40,000, admitted students, Feb 1).
first_frc_scholarship.deadline: February 1 (online application). For the Fall 2027 cycle this maps to 2027-02-01; the year is inferred from the published month/day. Admission must come first, so an EA application (decision by December 15) leaves time to apply.

decision_dates.notification_note: EA decisions come 'by December 15' per the international applicants page and CDS C16/C22; RD notification is March 15 per CDS C16. Both are treated as upper bounds, not promised release dates. Financial aid award notices: EA admits starting in January, RD admits in March.
decision_dates.deposit_deadline: 2027-05-01 (non-refundable enrollment deposit, credited toward tuition and fees)
decision_dates.restrictions: Early Action is non-binding; there is no Early Decision plan. An EA application missing materials at November 1 moves to Regular Decision. Rose-Hulman advises applying EA by November 1 for maximum scholarship consideration. Application opens August 1.

admissions.supplemental_essays_note: Rose-Hulman's first-year checklist lists the application, transcript, one recommendation and the fee (or waiver); no school-specific essay or supplement is listed on the deadlines, apply or Common App profile pages. Whether the Common App personal essay is required or optional for Rose-Hulman is not stated; CDS C7 still lists Application Essay as a factor. Confirm in the Common App or GoRose App before submitting.
why_us_ammunition: The Multidisciplinary Robotics Minor requires CSSE 120, ME/CSSE 435 Robotics Engineering and ECE 425 Introduction to Mobile Robotics; the Computer Engineering track adds CSSE 463 Image Recognition and ECE 320 Linear Control Systems.
The student Robotics team competes in the Intelligent Ground Vehicle Competition and MATE-ROV, with team space in the Branam Innovation Center.
Admission is to the institute, and changing majors goes through the Registrar with no published GPA or capacity limit.
admissions.cs_gate_basis: The catalog's Changing Curriculum rule says a student should 'notify the Registrar's office as soon as possible'; it lists no GPA or capacity limit for changing majors.

admission_structure.applies_to_note: Single first-year application to the institute through the GoRose App or the Common App; 'No preference is given for either of the application platforms for admission or scholarship purposes.'
units_named: n/a - no undergraduate colleges/schools that applicants select; an 'Undecided Major' option is available.
admission_structure.internal_mobility: Change of major: notify the Registrar's office as soon as possible; no GPA or capacity limit is listed. Undecided students take a common fall schedule and commit to a major during the first fall. This is not a guarantee of a seat in any specific course.

engineering.basis: Institute-level admission; Computer Engineering, EE and ME are declared without a published competitive gate. The catalog lists no GPA or capacity limit for changing majors.
engineering.how_you_enter: Apply to Rose-Hulman through the GoRose App or Common App (EA Nov 1 or RD Feb 1) with an intended major or Undecided; add the Multidisciplinary Robotics Minor after enrolling.

computing.basis: Computer Science and Software Engineering follow the same institute-level admission and Registrar change-of-major process; no published gate.
computing.how_you_enter: Apply to Rose-Hulman with CS or SE as the intended major, or change through the Registrar.

robotics_curriculum_detail.score_basis: 4/5: the EAC-accredited CPE degree requires embedded systems and, for robotics-minor students, linear controls; the minor's CPE track adds robotics engineering, mobile robotics and image recognition. Not a dedicated robotics degree.
robotics_curriculum_detail.count_note: Illustrative verified course options, not an exhaustive course count or a guarantee of enrollment. ME/CSSE 435 is one cross-listed course.
robotics_curriculum_detail.capstone: CPE majors take ECE 460/461/462 Engineering Design I-III (3+4+2 credits), a three-term client-driven design sequence. The current catalog lists the three-term Multidisciplinary Capstone (MDS 410/420/430) only in the minor's ENGD track; no separate robotics capstone is required for CPE.

robotics_ai.capstone: ECE 460/461/462 Engineering Design I-III: a client-driven project using a formal design process over three quarters (9 credits) (ROSE-R3, ROSE-HULMAN-E4). The robotics minor's CPE and EE tracks list no separate capstone; the three-term Multidisciplinary Capstone (MDS 410/420/430) appears only in the ENGD track (ROSE-R1).

door.how_you_enter: You apply to Rose-Hulman as an institution (one application, non-binding Early Action Nov 1 or Regular Decision Feb 1) and the application pages describe no separate ECE admitting unit. Students begin their chosen curriculum in the first year; the CPE plan starts ECE 160 in the first fall.
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Rose-Hulman's application page describes one institute-level process with no major-specific criteria, and no per-major admit rates are published (ROSE-HULMAN-E7). The catalog's changing-curriculum rule asks only that students notify the Registrar (ROSE-R12).

ece.vs_cs: CPE gives embedded systems, architecture, operating systems and controls; EE emphasizes circuits, signals and controls with more free CSSE room only through electives; CS (192 credits, new curriculum from Fall 2026) gives software and AI depth but needs ME 230 Mechatronic Systems from the minor for hardware. All three can take the robotics minor. The ECE department does not allow an EE + CPE double major.
ece.notable: BS EE and BS CPE each require 194 quarter credits (the EE sample plan totals 193). ECE offers the robotics minor, an ECE minor for other majors, power and communications certificates, and two master's degrees: MSEE (thesis, 48 credits) and MECE (course-based, 48 credits). BSEE/BSCPE area-elective credits cannot double-count toward the MSEE. The department reports a 'nearly 100 percent career placement rate.' (ROSE-HULMAN-E1, ROSE-HULMAN-E2, ROSE-HULMAN-E3, ROSE-R21)
ece.verification_note: Catalog program and course pages and ECE department pages retrieved October 16, 2026. Future course offerings and seats are not guaranteed.

undergrad_enrollment_note: Fall 2025 census from the 2025-26 Common Data Set (B1): 2,153 degree-seeking plus 7 non-degree undergraduates. cost_note: 2026-27 estimated first-year on-campus budget is $86,344: tuition and fees $59,772, housing and food $18,534, one-time first-year laptop bundle $2,800 (direct cost $81,106), plus books and supplies $1,200 and miscellaneous/transportation/additional food $4,038 (indirect cost $5,238). The page does not split tuition from fees or print a single grand total; $86,344 is the sum of the two published subtotals. Student health insurance is another $1,091 unless waived. No residency differential applies.

score_notes.cs_foundations: Programming and software foundations are assessed in the recommended B.S. in Robotics Engineering (new joint ECSE + MANE major, first class Fall 2026) plan. This is not the former CS/AI major; use the home-department core and the prerequisites on Robotics routes.
score_notes.math_foundations: Check calculus, linear algebra, probability and differential-equation preparation against the recommended engineering plan and the controls/learning prerequisites. Do not substitute the former CS/AI major requirements.
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: Supporting options for the recommended route: ECSE 4840 / ECSE 4850 / MANE 4962 Machine Learning / Deep Learning elective choice; CSCI 4270 Computational Vision. Prerequisites, permissions and degree credit restrictions are recorded on Robotics routes.
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Supporting AI is elective depth within B.S. in Robotics Engineering (new joint ECSE + MANE major, first class Fall 2026). ECSE 4840 / ECSE 4850 / MANE 4962 Machine Learning / Deep Learning elective choice; CSCI 4270 Computational Vision. Check the stated prerequisites, permissions and degree-credit rules; these courses are not all required or guaranteed.
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: The reviewed undergraduate options emphasize perception, machine learning and planning for robotics. Graduate institute topics or an alternative AI-major core are not counted as required coursework.
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: The recommended route has its own degree requirements, elective slots and minor-overlap rules. Confirm that each AI or robotics elective counts toward this specific degree; university-wide availability is insufficient.
score_notes.course_availability: Future course offerings, seats and permissions are not guaranteed; current catalogue listings and published annual/every-other-year categories are recorded separately.
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: URP pays a minimum $14.20/hr with up to $500/semester subsidized by the Office of Undergraduate Education, and the Summer Undergraduate Research Award pays up to $6,400 for 10 weeks open to all undergraduates [RPI-S18] [RPI-S20].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: URP is a structured faculty-matching program and the CS co-term requires a prospective MS advisor's letter describing a research project [RPI-S17] [RPI-S49], but AIRC and RAIR present as graduate-centered and no lab page lists undergraduate members.
score_notes.project_based_learning: Home-department design/capstone and documented robotics course projects support this route. Robotics work is anchored by the Center for Smart Convergent Manufacturing Systems (CSCMS), a Robotics Teaching Lab, and the MILL manufacturing lab with industrial robots; student groups include the RPI Robotics Club (combat robotics, drones, GVC projects) and the RPai AI club. A robotics lab or industry sponsor does not guarantee an undergraduate position.

admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025: 14,356 applicants, 9,655 admitted, 1,394 enrolled = 67.3% [RPI-S1]. New York residents 2,917/4,319 = 67.5%; out-of-state 6,125/8,947 = 68.5%; international 613/1,090 = 56.2% [RPI-S1] (INFERRED - division of CDS C1 counts). Residency is irrelevant here, and RPI is by far the least selective school in this batch on paper - the constraint is cost and yield (1,394 enrolled from 9,655 admits), which is why merit and FIRST scholarships matter more than admissibility.
admissions.major_admit_context: DIRECT primary ROBT major: official program invites incoming Class of 2030 to choose ROBT, with Fall 2026 first-year Introduction to Robotics. Current students may add or switch subject to program compatibility. Recommended route: B.S. in Robotics Engineering (new joint ECSE + MANE major, first class Fall 2026). University-wide rates are not major-specific admission probabilities.
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: CDS 2025-2026: 317 Early Decision applications, 219 admitted = 69.1% (INFERRED - division of CDS C21 counts) [RPI-S1]. The ED rate is essentially identical to the overall rate, so ED at RPI buys certainty and demonstrated commitment (which the CDS marks as Considered), not a statistical edge - and it forfeits the ability to compare aid offers.
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 records Early Action closing 12/1 with notification 1/29 but publishes no EA applicant/admit counts [RPI-S1].
admissions.test_detail_note: Fall 2025 enrolled: SAT submitted by 53% (733 students), ACT by 13% (180). SAT composite 25th/50th/75th = 1380/1450/1500; ACT 31/33/34 [RPI-S1]. Scores of admitted students are high relative to the admit rate - a strong score is the main merit-aid lever.
admissions.gpa_note: 43% of enrolled first-year students reported a 4.0 GPA; average high school GPA 3.93 with 96% submitting (CDS C11/C12) [RPI-S1]. Class rank: 63% top tenth, 90% top quarter [RPI-S1].
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: TEST-OPTIONAL, explicitly for this applicant's cycle: 'Any student who applies to attend Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute as an undergraduate in the fall of 2027 will be able to choose whether or not to submit SAT or ACT scores,' and 'RPI will remain test-optional through the Fall 2030 application cycle' [RPI-S3]. Mechanics: answer the Common App question 'Would you like RPI to consider your ACT/SAT scores as a part of your application file?'; if you say yes, the file is incomplete until scores arrive (official or self-reported); changes require emailing adm_updates@rpi.edu; Regular Decision applicants may use tests taken before January 31; 'not submitting test scores does not lower your chances of admission' and 'RPI does not use test scores to determine student eligibility for merit aid.' Exception: Physician-Scientist (B.S./M.D.) applicants must submit official scores [RPI-S3][RPI-S4].
admissions.c7_note: RPI is one of two schools in this batch that count level of applicant's interest (Considered) [RPI-S1] - campus visits, portal engagement, the optional GLIMPSE video and an ED application all register. Alumni relation Considered; interview, geographical residence, state residency and religious affiliation Not Considered [RPI-S1].

CSCI 4480 is the same course as ECSE 4480 and MANE 4560, and you cannot get credit for more than one. CSCI has only one robotics course, so robotics depth in CS is thin.

robotics_ai.concentration_name: ECSE optional Focus Areas: 'Robotics and Automation', 'Control Systems', 'Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning', 'Computer Vision and Image Processing' (RPI-E2)
robotics_ai.capstone: n.a. - ECSE's undergraduate program pages describe program templates and focus-area electives; a specific senior capstone course could not be confirmed from the pages fetched (RPI-E2, RPI-E7).

door.how_you_enter: RPI applicants either declare a specific major or apply undeclared to a school - the admissions FAQ lists 'Options for declaring a major: Declare specific major / Undeclared to a specific school (i.e., undeclared engineering)' - so ECSE is entered by major choice inside one engineering application rather than through a separate admitting college (RPI-E4).
door.easier_than_cs_basis: RPI's admissions FAQ pages describe major/undeclared options but publish no per-major admit rates; ECSE publishes enrollment and degree counts for accreditation purposes (e.g. Electrical Engineering 389 undergraduates in 19/20) but no admissions selectivity data (RPI-E4, RPI-E3).

ece.vs_cs: ECSE is the strongest robotics door at RPI because RPI has no standalone undergraduate robotics degree: robotics arrives as ECSE focus areas ('Robotics and Automation', 'Control Systems', 'Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning', 'Computer Vision and Image Processing'), and completing and declaring one earns a certificate at graduation (RPI-E2). Versus CS you gain circuits, signals, embedded hardware, power and control theory plus the EAC-accredited engineering credential; you give up depth in software systems and theory. RPI's dual-major mechanism makes ECSE+CS realistic - electives can 'Fulfill the course requirements of a dual major,' one diploma is awarded for both majors, and the 24-credit math/science and 24-credit HASS requirements count for both curricula (RPI-E2, RPI-E5).
ece.notable: Both ECSE undergraduate programs (Electrical Engineering and Computer and Systems Engineering) are separately EAC-accredited (RPI-E3); ECSE research includes 'cyberphysical systems such as smart grid and collaborative robots' (RPI-E1); dual major is administered via the registrar with a first-named and second-named major (RPI-E5); ECSE publishes per-class program templates and an undergraduate course flowchart (RPI-E7).

name: Worcester Polytechnic Institute (WPI)
degree_name: B.S. in Robotics Engineering (ABET-accredited primary major)
degree_type: Dedicated primary robotics engineering bachelor’s degree [WPI-R26-1][WPI-R26-4]
program_archetype: Primary robotics engineering with supporting AI
major_access_full: University admission followed by first-year major declaration, usually near the end of B Term. No separate competitive RBE declaration gate was found in the reviewed official guidance.
recommended_major_route: Apply intending BS Robotics Engineering, then declare during the first year. Keep its required hardware/controls/navigation base and add prepared undergraduate AI electives. [WPI-R26-1][WPI-R26-7]
alternative_route: BS Artificial Intelligence with the Robotics concentration, or BS ECE / CS + Robotics Engineering minor
primary_structural_risk: Seven-week course sequencing and elective prerequisites. RBE 4701 is Category II, offered at least every other year; future dates and seats are not assured.
notable_ai_institute: Department of Artificial Intelligence [WPI-S3]; PracticePoint (medical cyber-physical systems, surgical robotics, clinical data analytics) [WPI-S73]
notable_undergraduate_research_program: EREE — Early Research Experience in E-Term, $4,500/10 weeks, open to first- and second-years [WPI-S26]
fourplusone_name: WPI BS/MS program; BS/MS in Artificial Intelligence [WPI-S38][WPI-S6]
housing_guarantee: Required and guaranteed for first AND second years (Class of 2030 onward); not guaranteed for juniors/seniors [WPI-S51][WPI-S52]
greek_participation: 26% of men, 25% of women (CDS 2024-25); CONFLICTING third-party figure of 45% of women [WPI-S21][WPI-S37]
recreation_center: Sports & Recreation Center — Mon–Fri 6 a.m.–11 p.m., Sat 8 a.m.–11 p.m., Sun 10 a.m.–11 p.m., with pool [WPI-S33]
best_fit_reason: The Unified Robotics sequence integrates mechanics, sensing, manipulation and navigation. Embedded systems, statics, controls and an RBE design MQP build a hardware foundation; undergraduate AI and vision electives add autonomy.
biggest_concern: Private-school net cost and a fast term system. Advanced AI depth comes from chosen electives rather than being required throughout the robotics degree.
evidence_confidence: Official curriculum and entry sources reviewed October 14, 2026; recommendations and 1–5 scores are analyst assessments. Future seats, unpublished cohort rules and some source conflicts remain unresolved.

score_notes.cs_foundations: RBE requires 1 unit of CS including object-oriented programming and software engineering. CS 2223 algorithms is recommended preparation for AI/ML choices, rather than an attributed required AI-degree core.
score_notes.math_foundations: RBE requires at least 7/3 math units including differential/integral calculus, differential equations, linear algebra and probability.
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: Undergraduate RBE 4701 AI for Robotics, 4744 Deep Learning for Perception, 4540 Vision-based Manipulation and CS 4342 ML offer elective AI depth within a robotics-first degree.
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Supporting AI is elective depth within B.S. in Robotics Engineering (ABET-accredited primary major). RBE 4701 Artificial Intelligence for Robotics; RBE 4540 Vision-based Robotic Manipulation; RBE 4744 Deep Learning for Perception; CS 4342 Machine Learning. Check the stated prerequisites, permissions and degree-credit rules; these courses are not all required or guaranteed.
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: The reviewed undergraduate options emphasize perception, machine learning and planning for robotics. Graduate institute topics or an alternative AI-major core are not counted as required coursework.
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: The recommended route has its own degree requirements, elective slots and minor-overlap rules. Confirm that each AI or robotics elective counts toward this specific degree; university-wide availability is insufficient.
score_notes.course_availability: 2026–27 UG catalog: RBE 4744/4540/CS 4342 at least annually (Category I), RBE 4701 at least every other year (Category II). Rotation does not guarantee future terms or seats.
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: EREE pays $4,500 over 10 weeks and is aimed at first- and second-year students with a faculty-matching committee, and the CUR submission states 100% of full-time faculty involve undergraduates in research [WPI-S26][WPI-S14].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: The required 9-credit MQP gives every senior a faculty-advised research project, and A&S research pages name individual undergraduate fellows with their advisors (e.g., a CS+RBE double major with Prof. Whitehill) [WPI-S12][WPI-S27].
score_notes.project_based_learning: RBE 3001 builds/programs a vision-guided manipulator; RBE 3002 uses an open-ended navigation lab; RBE 2020 develops real robot electronics; MQP must be RBE capstone design.
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: Primary RBE BS: required 2001/2002/3001/3002 or equivalent, embedded systems, statics and classical controls, and RBE capstone MQP; AI depth is elective.
score_notes.computing_resources: No public GPU inventory or undergraduate cluster-access policy was found; PracticePoint provides physical labs rather than compute [WPI-S73][WPI-S74].
score_notes.industry_preparation: General programme preparation context; CS salaries, company bands and graduate institute research are not verified robotics-major placement outcomes. Confirm the selected degree’s graduate option and any eligible co-op/research pathway.
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: General programme preparation context; CS salaries, company bands and graduate institute research are not verified robotics-major placement outcomes. Confirm the selected degree’s graduate option and any eligible co-op/research pathway.
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: General programme preparation context; CS salaries, company bands and graduate institute research are not verified robotics-major placement outcomes. Confirm the selected degree’s graduate option and any eligible co-op/research pathway.
score_notes.intellectual_energy: Students across five independent threads describe 35–45 hour academic weeks in a collaborative atmosphere, with 91% first-to-second-year retention [WPI-S63][WPI-S59][WPI-S11].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: The registrar awards only A, B, C or NR, and NR does not appear on transcripts or grade reports — removing the mechanical basis for grade competition [WPI-S15][WPI-S11].
score_notes.student_agency: Eleven AI concentrations including "Design Your Own"-style breadth options, HECCMA cross-registration, and student-initiated events like the club-run PLAnt competition with 26 robots [WPI-S1][WPI-S67][WPI-S47].
score_notes.community_within_scale: 93% of first-years live on campus, first- and second-year residency is now required for the Class of 2030, and IQP project centers place 24–28 students abroad with two resident faculty [WPI-S21][WPI-S51][WPI-S12].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: 15 robotics/technology clubs demonstrated at the 2025-09-09 Robotics Clubs Showcase, and the Robotics Club ran its own 26-robot combat event on 2025-09-26 [WPI-S46][WPI-S47].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: No student-organization directory was retrieved in this session; only technical clubs were verified [WPI-S46][WPI-S47].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Greek participation is high for a tech school (26% of men, 25% of women per CDS) and students report thin Worcester nightlife outside Greek/house parties, though a strong LGBTQ community is also described [WPI-S21][WPI-S59][WPI-S60].
score_notes.campus_engagement: Required first- and second-year residency plus Innovation Studio hours to midnight weeknights and 1 a.m. weekends indicate an evening-active campus [WPI-S51][WPI-S31].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: Sports & Recreation Center opens at 6 a.m. weekdays and closes at 11 p.m. daily, with a pool and posted membership terms [WPI-S33][WPI-S34].
score_notes.daily_life: Campus is 1.5 miles from Union Station with MBTA commuter rail to Boston (~$11.50 each way per students) and free SNAP evening shuttles, but Boston is an hour away and Worcester nightlife is reported as limited [WPI-S55][WPI-S57][WPI-S60].

WPI was test-blind 2021-2024 and returned to test-optional beginning with the Class of 2030 (Fall 2026 entry) per a November 2024 faculty Committee on Academic Policy motion; WPI describes it as a 'no-harm' practice and asks on the Common Application whether scores should be considered.

interview.mechanism: No evaluative admissions interview; CDS C7 marks Interview 'Not Considered'. WPI will, however, 'consider Initialview or Vericant interviews if submitted' from international applicants as a supplement to English-proficiency evidence.

first_frc_scholarship.name: WPI Design Innovation Scholarship; WPI FIRST Community Scholarship; FIRST Digital Animation Award (WPI also offers VEX/REC Foundation Aerial Drone awards)
first_frc_scholarship.amount: Design Innovation Scholarship: one full-tuition four-year award (~$220,000) plus three $40,000 awards ($10,000/year). FIRST Community Scholarship: one full-tuition four-year award (~$220,000). FIRST Digital Animation Award: $1,000 scholarship to any student on a submitting team. Full-tuition awards increase as tuition increases.
first_frc_scholarship.application_mechanism: Complete the WPI admissions application by the February 1 Regular Decision deadline, then submit the separate scholarship application form with a signed adult mentor/coach nomination and a video of five minutes or less. Eligibility is limited to FRC, FTC and FIRST Global participants (FLL excluded), one nominee per team per scholarship, final year of high school, active member of the current season's team.
first_frc_scholarship.deadline: For the 2026-27 cycle the applications opened December 15, 2025 and closed February 23, 2026 (11:59 PM EST), with mentor nominations due March 2, 2026, initial offers at the end of March and final notifications April 15, 2026. WPI states applications reopen in Fall 2026 for the next cycle.

ece.vs_cs: WPI already has an EAC-accredited Robotics Engineering degree, so ECE is not the robotics door here — it is the hardware-depth door: circuits, microelectronics, embedded computing, signals, control systems and power that neither CS nor the interdisciplinary RBE core covers to the same depth (WPI-E5, WPI-E4). What ECE costs you relative to RBE is the integrated robotics core itself (manipulation, mechanics, robot software stack), and relative to CS you trade algorithms/software breadth for circuit and signal depth. WPI's structure makes doubling up cheap in principle: the Robotics Engineering page lists Electrical & Computer Engineering among potential minors, and ECE offers a minor with clusters in control and power, signals, analog and RF (WPI-E6, WPI-E2) — but WPI does not publish how many students actually pair RBE with an ECE major, so treat 'commonly double up' as unverified.
ece.notable: ECE offers a BS/MS in five years and an ECE minor with clusters in control and power, signals, analog and RF (WPI-E2); the ECE department in Atwater Kent Laboratories lists research in machine learning, signal processing, autonomous vehicles, prosthetic control and microelectronics (WPI-E1); WPI's engineering accreditation page confirms both 'electrical and computer engineering' and 'robotics engineering' programs are EAC-accredited (WPI-E4).

cost_note: 2026-27 first-year on-campus budget is $87,570: tuition $63,936, fees $1,502, housing $10,660, food $9,072, books $1,200, personal $1,200. The published resident transportation line is not applicable; required health insurance costs another $2,945 unless waived.
